News.title: Where is Alejandra Mendoza now? The true story behind A Child of My Own on Netflix
News.content:
MAITE Alberdi’s new Netflix documentary A Child of My Own tells the story of one of the most unusual criminal cases in recent Mexican history.

It portrays the real life events and actions carried out by Eleonor Alejandra Marín Mendoza, who took desperate measures in order to enact her dream of being a mother.



How did Alejandra Mendoza end up in jail?

In 2008, Mendoza (known as Ale) was 25 years old and facing pressure from her loved ones to become a mother, having just suffered a series of miscarriages.

After her third loss, Mendoza was pushed to the limit and decided to fake a pregnancy by deliberately gaining weight, lying to her family and husband, Arturo, for months.



Across this time, she faked medical reports and went on maternity leave after attending an appointment with her husband where a doctor attempted to listen for the heartbeat of the “baby”.

When her “due date” came along in June 2009, she was arrested for stealing a newborn baby from a New Mexico hospital in an act of desperation, shocking the entire country.



Despite claiming she had permission from the mother of the infant, she and Arturo were ultimately convicted of kidnapping – although the latter claimed to know nothing about the act.

Arturo was eventually acquitted following his trial, having already served two years and six months in prison for initially being considered an accomplice to his wife.

“I was drawn into problems that got bigger and bigger,” says Ale in the documentary.

“And I started making decisions and taking actions which got more complicated, until there was no way out. No turning back.”



Where is Alejandra Mendoza now?

A Child of My Own was released on Netflix on Thursday, August 13 after making its world premiere at the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival back in February.

The film has a runtime of just over an hour-and-a-half, with the story centring around the real-life crime committed by Eleonor Alejandra Marín Mendoza.

Directed by two-time Oscar nominated documentary filmmaker Maite Alberdi, her latest project is staged as a cinematic ‘docudrama’ for the first half of the film, with Ana Celeste portraying Mendoza.



It then structurally changes at the halfway mark, with the second half shifting to a more traditional documentary as it shows real life encounters of Mendoza being interviewed in a Mexican jail, whilst also presenting first-hand testimonies and court reports of the case.

Upon meeting her, director Alberdi said: “Alejandra wasn’t someone I would have imagined ending up in prison.

“I was struck by how extraordinary everything she told me was.”

Mendoza had to spend 13 years, three months, and 25 days in jail.

In the last few weeks of her sentence she completed the interview which is shown in the film.



She was released from prison in 2023, and currently lives as a free woman in Mexico.

She said: “During my thirteen years in prison, I have focused on accepting not being a mum.”

“Before, I think my desire to be a mum was more about pleasing others. What else is out there beyond being a mum?

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But I finally realised there’s so much more to live for.”

The documentary shows that Mendoza and her husband Arturo reconciled and are now back together, after initially separating while she was serving time.

News.title: Can I still have a barbecue in my garden? The Government ban on disposable BBQs explained
News.content:
THE government has made the decision to temporarily BAN disposable barbecues due to the “significant risk” they present.

It comes after a series of wildfires across the UK – but what are the rules and safety recommendations around using a standard barbecue this summer?



Can I still have a BBQ in my garden?

The government order issued on Friday August 14 states: “The government considers that the supply and subsequent foreseeable use of disposable barbecues poses a significant risk to the public, and the environment, and therefore cannot be considered a safe product.

“They should not be made available for supply either in store or online at the current time.”



These guidelines refer specifically to barbecues that are domestic, single-use only, and not intended for re-filling or reuse.

They comprise of a fuel tray, grill grid and include charcoal fuel sufficient to provide the necessary cooking temperature for the duration of a single cooking session.

Retailers and distributors have been informed not to sell the products, with “criminal sanctions” put in place for those who don’t comply.

The government advises that the ban is set to remain in place until weather conditions change sufficiently to reduce the level of risk, and “will be withdrawn in consultation with relevant departments and agencies”.

There is currently no formal, nationwide guidance in place relating to permanent, non-disposable home barbecues designed for repeated use.

However, various councils and fire services around the country have issued guidance around using your barbecue safely.



What are the key barbecue safety tips?

Location

The first step in ensuring you have a safe barbecue is setting it up in an appropriate location.

As per the Norwich City Council, it should always be placed on a flat, stable level, ground, and never be placed directly onto dry grass, vegetation or a balcony of any kind.

Also remember to keep it well away from any sheds, fences, trees, plants and anything else that could a fire.

Finally, make sure to have safety equipment ready by your side, that being either a bucket of water, a bucket of sand or a garden hose.



Concentration

Another important factor in making sure you are in full control of your barbecue is to have maximum concentration.

To do so, make sure to never leave the barbecue unattended, even for just a small amount of time, while it’s still lit or hot.

Also be sure to keep children, pets, and any form of garden game well away from the cooking zone.

Finally, the London Fire Brigade states that the person manning the barbecue should never drink too much alcohol, as that can often slow reaction time and cause costly errors.



Finishing up…

Once the cooking is finished, wait until the barbecue has cooled down and make sure the embers and ashes have been fully extinguished.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

From that point, empty the ash onto bare soil, and as the Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service points out, remember to never to discard them straight into a dustbin.

And be aware that smouldering ashes can give off dangerous carbon monoxide fumes.

News.title: Brutal world of dolphin shows with tormented ‘self-harming’ animals crammed into tiny concrete tanks and kicked by kids
News.content:
COVERED in scars and visibly distressed, a bottlenose dolphin poses for photos with tourists before being forced to perform tricks to a cheering crowd.

Later, they’re returned to a tiny concrete tank, where loud music blares constantly. This is the brutal reality behind Europe’s dolphin shows, with unwitting Brit tourists paying to watch them.



It is estimated that more than 3,700 whales and dolphins are being held captive across 345 facilities in 56 countries around the world – many snatched from the wild for entertainment, with bottlenose dolphins the most commonly held species.

Confined to tiny tanks, the animals can become so distressed that they self-harm – including slamming their heads against their enclosures, teeth grinding and refusing to eat – with animal rights campaigners describing their existence as a “living death”.

While the UK’s last Dolphinarium closed its doors in March 1993 and Canada, Chile, India and Costa Rica also banning dolphin shows, many European countries still allow them – and continue to flog tickets to the public, including Brits.



Scores of celebs, including Kim Kardashian, Kimberley Walsh and Wayne and Coleen Rooney, have also faced criticism for paying to swim or pose with dolphins on luxury trips.

PETA’s Vice President of Programmes Elisa Allen says: “These bright, complex, ocean-going mammals experience living death in tiny cement boxes and, unlike the tourists whose money keeps these attractions running, they never get to leave.

“Instead of exploring vast stretches of ocean, caring for their young, forming lifelong bonds, and conversing with each other, captive dolphins are forced to perform tawdry tricks and subjected to noise, stress and unwanted human handling.

“PETA urges everyone to keep their money in their pockets or risk keeping these pits of animal misery afloat.”

In the wild, dolphins can roam freely in territories spanning more than 100km, but in captivity, they are often confined to tanks of less than 5,000 square feet.



According to PETA, the result can lead to severe mental distress, with dolphins displaying repetitive behaviours, such as head bobbing and pacing.

In May, horrifying drone footage was shared of six dolphins at The Hyatt Ziva Cancún resort, where the former swimming pool is rented to dolphin experience company, Delphinus.

The dolphins were seen floating listlessly, and swimming in circles.



While Mexico is one country to ban dolphin shows, due to a 18-month legal transition phase which ends later this year, dolphins are still being held captive.

“These dolphins are in shallow tanks, have no escape, no shade, suffer from a constant barrage of disco music, and then at night a laser show keeps them awake,” says Marketa Schusterova, co-founder of animal rights group TideBreaker, who captured the footage.

“They are not medically looked after well, appear thin, have damage and scars on their bodies, and they are clearly distressed.”

Responding to the claims, a spokesperson for Hyatt Ziva Cancún previously said a third party Delphinus was responsible for the creatures, saying: “We understand the concerns raised regarding the dolphins at the resort.

“Delphinus is an organisation accredited by Mexican authorities and international agencies and is responsible for the care of the dolphins, including support from trained animal care and veterinary professionals.”



Palmitos Park in Gran Canaria, which has six male dolphins, has also come under fire from tourists who claim they witnessed trainers dragging the mammals and allowing children to kick them.

One visitor said: “The dolphins were in the pools with the tiniest amount of space to roam free and in the show they looked uncomfortable.”

Another said: “The dolphins were made to take pictures with the public for up to 40 mins before the show, the trainers towards the end were dragging the dolphins by their mouths to get them into position, one kid actually kicked the dolphin twice.”

Another park using the animals for entertainment is Loro Parque, Tenerife, which advertises trick shows with their dolphins Pacina, Luna, Ilse, Clara, Achille, Ulisse and Ebu.

With 2.7million Brits visiting Tenerife each year, many are likely to visit the park, probably not knowing the true scale of alleged cruelty behind the shows.



In 2023, The Dolphin Project publicly criticised the way the 33-acre wildlife park and zoo treated and paraded its aquatic mammals in front of an 1,800-capacity theatre.



The performances were said to include dolphins jumping over poles, spinning on platforms and balancing upside down in the water while waving their tail flukes at the audience.

In one shocking stunt, trainers would even use the dolphins as ‘ride-on toys’, which PETA has warned can cause serious harm and damage to the creatures, including impairing their hearing.

Dolphin encounters are not just popular with tourists – celebrities have also helped give the controversial attractions a glossy image by posing for pictures and swimming alongside the animals.

Reality TV star Sam Faiers found herself at the centre of a social media storm some time ago, after posting pictures of herself and her family taking part in a Dolphins Emotions swim experience at the controversial Zoomarine in Guia, Portugal in 2016.

The park had faced animal welfare allegations, including claims that dolphins were made to tow a small boat carrying children around the pool and were used as selfie props, with visitors able to kiss, hug and stroke them.



Speaking at the time, Sam defended the experience, saying: “To me they were being well looked after and fed, they had the biggest swimming pool to swim in.”

However, Zoomarine has since appeared on World Animal Protection’s list of 12 zoos globally to avoid.

The £950million Atlantis, The Palm on Dubai’s glitzy Palm Jumeirah is another celebrity hotspot for dolphin encounters.

When the mega-resort opened its doors in 2008, it pulled in a glittering crowd of celebs and royals, including Oprah Winfrey and The Duchess of York, but its dolphins soon became the centre of a storm over animals being used for entertainment.

Danny Groves from Whale and Dolphin Conservation, says: “There is no ethical reason in today’s world to keep dolphins and whales imprisoned in a concrete tank for their entire, shortened lives where they are forced to perform tricks to entertain us.



“What people who go to these shows often do not realise is the cruelty that their ticket money helps to perpetuate.”

And it appears attitudes are changing towards using dolphins as tourist attractions.

For example, UK holiday firms Jet2 and Easyjet have ended ticket sales to marine parks and other attractions offering dolphin experiences – while TUI has come under fire for not doing the same.

News.title: Tate brothers ‘drinking dirty brown shower water’ and are woken by ‘demonic roar’ of inmates in hellhole prison
News.content:
ANDREW and Tristan have complained about being held in a hellhole jail with “brown and filthy” shower water, where the sounds of “demonic roars” wake them up every night.

Andrew, 39, and brother Tristan, 38, have been locked up since their arrest at a bare-knuckle boxing event in Miami on July 18.



The brothers have been charged with rape, sex trafficking and offences related to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

They are now being held in Florida’s Miami Federal Detention Center, where their lawyers claim they are suffering in the harsh conditions.



Self-described misogynist Andrew called his Special Housing Unit (SHU) “punitive housing for people who murder their cellmates“.

The dual US-UK citizen claimed he had been forced to drink unclean water that made him sick.



His only water source is a shower and a “brown and filthy faucet” which has left him suffering “persistent stomach problems”, he claims.

The jail has faced cooling and water problems and a clash between inmates and staff in recent months, according to the US Bureau of Prisons.

It comes as court documents revealed that the brothers held several passports under different aliases – including one name borrowed from a Bond villain.

Andrew said he had been woken up in the middle of the night by other prisoners yelling death threats and had heard a “demonic roar” from a neighbouring cell.



He also claimed he was staying in “the worst possible conditions the US gov provides to terrorists and psychopaths”, adding that the inmate in the neighbouring cell was a “cannibal who screams throughout the night”.

In another message on X, Andrew complained he had “no commissary. No visits. No contact with the outside world.”

He ranted: “I am an innocent until proven guilty extradition detainee. I’m wanted by a foreign state. I am an American citizen. WHY AM I HERE?”



Their lawyers claimed they had not been let out of their cells at all for 11 of their first 15 days in the jail.

Insiders told The Sun the conditions were a “disgrace”.

Last year, a report said inmates were forced to kneel and eat “like dogs”, with their hands shackled and food on chairs in front of them.

Toilets bubbling over with waste, crumbling infrastructure and an extreme use of force were also alleged by inmates’ families.

And as downtown Miami faces extreme heat, climbing above 30C, detainees say they have been left without air conditioning.



The facility has been blighted by AC issues for years, according to a 2020 report.

Inmates say they strip to their underwear amid the sweltering conditions and sweat through their sheets at night.

The brothers are fighting extradition to the UK, where they face a total of 59 criminal charges, including rape, sex trafficking and offenses related to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

Allegations against them include having sex with a minor, trafficking minors, running an organised crime operation and money laundering.

British prosecutors said new charges were fast-tracked after authorities investigated claims made by another four victims.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Andrew and Tristan both deny the charges and say they have done no wrongdoing.

A prison spokesperson told The Sun that inmates generally have access to commissary services, recreation, phone calls, social visits and legal counsel.

News.title: Woke plan to BAN white people from public pool sparks outrage and claims of ‘segregation’
News.content:
POOL FURY Woke plan to BAN white people from public pool sparks outrage and claims of ‘segregation’

A WOKE plan to ban white swimmers from a public pool in Berlin has sparked outrage and claims of segregation.

The Volksbühne theatre was given £255,000 of taxpayers’ money to open a “people’s swimming pool” that was supposed to be “open for all who are seeking to cool down in the increasingly hot Berlin summers”.



But the theatre advertised a six-hour event on Friday, August 14, when the 80ft open-air pop-up would be open “exclusively to black communities”.

The event, organised in partnership with the anti-discrimination group Each One Teach One, was due to shut the pool to the wider public from noon until 6pm.



Visitors were also asked to respect “this collective self-designation and the spaces associated with it”.

The decision sparked political backlash, with critics accusing organisers of turning a publicly funded facility into a racially divided space.



Stefan Evers, Berlin’s finance minister and Christian Democrat candidate for mayor, said: “I don’t believe in dividing people by skin colour.”

He added: “I understood the ‘People’s Swimming Pool’ as a swimming pool for everyone.”

Christoph Meyer, the centre-right Free Democratic Party candidate, also blasted the move.

He said: “Public spaces must bring society together, not segregate people based on skin colour.”



The event has now been cancelled, after the theatre complained it had become the “target of right-wing and racist incitement”.

Each One Teach One said it had received threatening and racist emails.

It added that could no longer guarantee the “physical and psychological safety” of the young people the event was intended for.



The theatre’s director, Matthias Lilienthal, has said he intends to rebook the event and will appear at the pool to discuss the controversy with members of the public.

The temporary pool, installed outside the city centre, is due to remain in place for eight weeks and is free for all guests.

The €300,000 (£256,000) project can accommodate just 46 swimmers at a time, with organisers estimating around 20,000 visitors during its run.

Lilienthal has said he hoped to give Berliners somewhere to swim as the city’s pool facilities face mounting pressure.

He told German broadcaster ZDF: “Half of the indoor and outdoor pools are closed, so we thought we’d help out Governing Mayor Kai Wegner.”



“The Volksbuhne considers even something as simple as two people splashing each other to be a theatrical event.”

The controversy comes during a sweltering summer in Germany, where extreme heat has placed further pressure on public swimming facilities.

Swimming pools have also increasingly become flashpoints for culture wars.

Last week, a swimming spot in Halle faced criticism after bathers were reportedly told they had to speak fluent German or risk being refused entry.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The pool said the rule was intended to help keep swimmers safe and ensure they could understand instructions.



Berlin’s swimming pools also introduced ID requirements in 2025 after a string of punch-ups and sexual harassment during hot summer days.

News.title: Lads land in hot water after being filmed using moving pickup truck as a mobile SWIMMING POOL to beat 31C heat
News.content:
THREE lads have landed themselves in hot water after turning a pickup truck into a bizarre pool on wheels.

Two shirtless pals were filmed sipping drinks and tucking into watermelon while cruising through the streets of Xining, China, as the city baked in 31C temps.



The yellow pickup was seen driving through town with its rear cargo bed filled with water and held in place by a plastic sheet.

The pair lounged in the makeshift pool as their third friend drove through the city in Qinghai Province on August 12.



The stunt quickly went viral on social media – with some users amused by the peculiar stunt.

But their DIY pool party soon attracted the attention of traffic police.

Officers spotted the online clip and swung into action, tracking the truck’s route using CCTV and launching a search.

They eventually stopped the mobile pool at the junction in the city’s Chengdong district yesterday.

The truck was classed as a freight vehicle, which are banned from carrying passengers under Chinese road laws.

Xining traffic police said the cargo bed had no seats, seatbelts or safety barriers.



They warned that sudden braking, sharp turns or bumps could have sent the pool pals flying out or even cause drowning.

Police said that it was not just the passengers at risk, as the water shifted the vehicle’s centre of gravity and made it unstable to drive.

Officers described the set-up as a “mobile bomb” and accused the culprits of treating public roads like a showground in a bid for online clout.



They urged drivers not to put social media fame above the safety of their lives.

Police seized the pick-up on the spot, fined the driver £110 (CNY 1,000) and hit him with three penalty points on his licence.

Officers also gave the two passengers a stern talking-to

News.title: Lucy Letby’s doctor ‘boyfriend’ found dead in car – after being ‘sacked over texts about her attempted murder of baby’
News.content:
DEATH RIDDLE Lucy Letby’s doctor ‘boyfriend’ found dead in car – after being ‘sacked over texts about her attempted murder of baby’

LUCY Letby’s “boyfriend” died on the anniversary of her arrest after reportedly being sacked for sending texts about a baby she attempted to murder.

The doctor – in his 50s and who The Sun first revealed last week had died suddenly – was found dead in his car on the eighth anniversary of the nurse’s first arrest on July 3, 2018.



The doctor was hauled before a disciplinary hearing in June over a series of inappropriate texts he sent the former neo-natal nurse while they worked together at the Countess of Chester Hospital, reports the Daily Mail.

The messages are understood to have breached patient confidentiality.



They are reported to have involved details of the care of a premature baby boy with haemophilia, known only as Baby N – who Letby was found guilty of attempting to murder.

Letby – held at HMP Bronzefield in Surrey – had called him her “best friend” and “love” in notes found at her home, and the pair swapped more than 1,300 Facebook messages.

The doctor – referred to as Doctor A in court due to reporting restrictions – had been ill before his death and his funeral has been held.

Cheshire Police, which has faced criticism over its handling of the case, refused to provide usual details after the registrar’s death.



And a listing for his death appeared to have been removed from the coroner’s website.

It is understood the doctor struggled with work issues following Letby’s August 2023 conviction.

He worked with Letby at the Countess of Chester Hospital at the time of her killing spree between June 2015 and June 2016 and supported her after she was moved from the neonatal unit amid fears over infant deaths.



Prosecutors referred to the medic as her “boyfriend” and said she was infatuated with him – suggesting he had provided a level of motivation for her crimes.

They alleged she created crisis situations by attacking babies, knowing he would be bleeped and dash to attend.

Letby denied being “in love” with the doctor and insisted they were “trusted” friends.

The charges Letby has been convicted of in full Child A, allegation of murder. The Crown said Letby injected air intravenously into the bloodstream of the baby boy. COUNT 1 GUILTY. Child B, allegation of attempted murder. The Crown said Letby attempted to murder the baby girl, the twin sister of Child A, by injecting air into her bloodstream. COUNT 2 GUILTY. Child C, allegation of murder. Prosecutors said Letby forced air down a feeding tube and into the stomach of the baby boy. COUNT 3 GUILTY. Child D, allegation of murder. The Crown said air was injected intravenously into the baby girl. COUNT 4 GUILTY. Child E, allegation of murder. The Crown said Letby murdered the twin baby boy with an injection of air into the bloodstream and also deliberately caused bleeding to the infant. COUNT 5 GUILTY. Child F, allegation of attempted murder. Letby was said by prosecutors to have poisoned the twin brother of Child E with insulin. COUNT 6 GUILTY. Child I, allegation of murder. The prosecution said Letby killed the baby girl at the fourth attempt and had given her air and overfed her with milk. COUNT 12 GUILTY. Child K, allegation of attempted murder. The prosecution said Letby compromised the baby girl as she deliberately dislodged a breathing tube. COUNT 14 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT AT ORIGINAL TRIAL, NOW GUILTY AFTER RETRIAL Child L, allegation of attempted murder. The Crown said the nurse poisoned the twin baby boy with insulin. COUNT 15 GUILTY. Child M, allegation of attempted murder. Prosecutors said Letby injected air into the bloodstream of Child L’s twin brother. COUNT 16 GUILTY. Child N, three allegations of attempted murder. The Crown said Letby inflicted trauma in the baby boy’s throat and also injected him with air in the bloodstream. COUNT 17 GUILTY, COUNT 18 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT, COUNT 19 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT. Child O, allegation of murder. Prosecutors say Letby attacked the triplet boy by injecting him with air, overfeeding him with milk and inflicting trauma to his liver with “severe force”. COUNT 20 GUILTY. Child P, allegation of murder. Prosecutors said the nurse targeted the triplet brother of Child O by overfeeding him with milk, injecting air and dislodging his breathing tube. COUNT 21 GUILTY. Child Q, allegation of attempted murder. The Crown said Letby injected the baby boy with liquid, and possibly air, down his feeding tube. COUNT 22 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT

But she called him “sweetie” in messages and broke down in tears when he entered the dock to give evidence against her.

When he gave evidence, the doctor did so from behind a screen to protect his anonymity.



At the later Thirlwall Inquiry in 2024, the doctor said he had been “misled” and “maybe manipulated” by Letby.

He said he had been tricked by her into giving her information about babies she had attacked.

He added: “I wasn’t aware of the full clinical picture and I provided support by being misled and maybe manipulated, and for that I’m really sorry.



“I have a lot of regrets about how that period of time took place.”

Letby is serving a whole-life tariff but maintains her innocence over the deaths of babies in 2015 and 2016.

She was found guilty of of murdering seven and attempting to kill seven more, one twice.

Letby lost two bids in 2024 to challenge her convictions.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the Criminal Cases Review Commission is considering evidence presented by a panel of doctors claiming that natural causes and poor care were to blame.

A spokesperson for Sodexo, which runs Bronzefield, did not comment.

News.title: M&S urgently pulls kitchen item from shelves with customers warned ‘stop using immediately’
News.content:
MARKS & SPENCER has issued an urgent recall over a kitchen essential with customers told to stop using it “immediately”.

The retail giant has now withdrawn the product from all online and in-store “sites”.

Customers have been urged to stop using M&S’s Hand Painted Jug following concerns from Office for Product Safety and Standards.



The agency said the product presented “a risk of injuries as the glass may break during use”, which could harm those attempting to use it.



The blue tinted jug features painted leaf decorations and was originally manufactured in China, with the batch number T34/9829D.

However, the Office for Product Safety and Standards has now found the item does not “meet the requirements of the General Product Safety Regulations 2005”.

M&S has added that it “identified a potential safety issue” with the product and recommended shoppers to “stop using the product immediately”.

As a result, the kitchen accessory has been withdrawn from sale in all in-store and online “sites”.

The retailer apologised for any inconvenience caused and said customers will be able to return the jug to any M&S site (excluding franchise and outlet stores) for a full refund.

Those with further questions will be able to contact the Customer Support team for help and support.

The jug had been sold in Fashion, Home & Beauty section of UK and ROI stores since February this year.



Priced at £18 (€23), the item has been removed from shelves from early August.

News.title: Temporary ban on sale of disposable BBQs over wildfire risk
News.content:
A total of 1,017 wildfires have been recorded in England and Wales this year, according to data shared by the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC), which matches last year's record.

Disposable barbecues "cannot be considered a safe product" in the current conditions and they "must not be made available for sale either in store or online at the current time" in Great Britain, according to the advice published by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST)., external

The ban applies to England, Scotland and Wales, but not Northern Ireland.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the measures were "common-sense steps to protect lives and the environment."

All retailers will be receiving guidance about the change, which will be kept under review, Burnham told the BBC.

Burnham also said some of the wildfires burning across the country will have been started by disposable barbecues.

Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live's Matt Chorley, the prime minister said: "We've got 37 fires across England and Wales right now, four of them are major incidents."

He added: "We're going into a difficult weekend, please just think about the situation that we're in.

"Britain is a tinderbox right now. Setting a fire in any outdoor setting of any kind is a risk to other people's homes, it's a risk to other people's lives, don't do it, please don't do it."

Many large retailers and supermarkets had already voluntarily stopped selling the devices under a framework agreed in 2023, external between fire chiefs and the British Retail Consortium.

It said that retailers should suspend sales once an extreme heat event has been declared as imminent, or in response to "reasonable, evidence based" requests from local councils.

David Skaith, the elected Labour mayor for York and North Yorkshire who has been campaigning for a ban on single-use grills, urged the prime minister to make it permanent.

He told the BBC: "We know the risks that disposable barbecues have been causing and to have a ban on them is much-needed, much-called-for and I hope it becomes long-term."

News.title: Chris Mason: Where does this unorthodox by-election victory leave Nigel Farage?
News.content:
It is a question prompting at least some debate within the party.

"When he goes down this angry route he doesn't help himself," the prominent Reform activist Tim Montgomerie told Radio 4's The World At One.

Montgomerie, the founder of the ConservativeHome website, defected to Reform two years ago. He praised Farage's political ability but added: "It's very frustrating how he's behaved today. He needs to get a grip of this problem."

Montgomerie argued Farage and Reform were at their best when they were more positive rather than "inward looking" and focused on "grievances."

The "grievances," as Montgomerie puts it, are real and legitimate, say Farage's friends.

In the short term at least and from a point of weakness I have previously written about, the by-election allowed Farage to get on the front foot and to frame an argument, as he saw it, as the people versus those out to get him.

Rubbish, say his critics, the rules apply to all MPs and the undeclared Â£5m gift from the billionaire businessman Christopher Harborne, in the months before Farage became an MP, should have been registered, they insist.

Talking to GB News in the early hours of this morning, before the result, Farage repeated a concession, of sorts, about this: "If I made one sin, it's that I haven't filled in a piece of paper.

"I've broken no law, I've broken no tax law, I've taken no public money. I don't even own a motor home. Maybe I haven't filled in a piece of paper. I'm confident I'm right - we'll see where we go."

He has long maintained he sought legal advice about whether he needed to declare the money and had been told he didn't.

The wider question is where Nigel Farage and Reform find themselves in the big picture politically and whether their current approach is a wise one.

There is early evidence of something of a Burnham bounce for Labour, which has disrupted Reform's long standing lead in the opinion polls.

And the Conservatives appear more chipper and competitive than a year ago too.

Then there is the rise of Restore Britain, run by the former Reform MP Rupert Lowe.

Let's be clear: none of the political parties are wildly popular at the moment, but Reform's support has shrivelled a bit and their rivals are more upbeat.

The landscape for the new political season at Westminster is taking shape, ahead of MPs returning to the Commons in a few weeks.

Labour with a spring in its step, for now at least. Reform punchy but feeling under the cosh and plenty of the others scrapping for attention too.

It will be a fascinating few months ahead.

News.title: Britain's Finlay Tarling dies in Volta a Portugal accident
News.content:
British cyclist Finlay Tarling has died aged 19, after a serious accident during the eighth stage of the Volta a Portugal.

Tarling is the younger brother of Netcompany Ineos rider Josh and had raced for Great Britain on the road and track.

The Welshman was competing for the NSN Development Team, when the incident occurred on the 166.8km route from Melgaco to Fafe.

In a statement, NSN said: "We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal today.

"Fin was a much loved member of our team but most importantly, he was a son, a brother, and a friend to so many. He will be deeply missed.

"Our deepest condolences go out to Fin's parents Michael and Dawn, his brother Josh, and everyone who was lucky enough to call Fin a friend."

In a post on X, the race organisers and the Portuguese Cycling Federation also expressed their "most heartfelt condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his team-mates, to the NSN Development Team, and to all his friends and loved ones".

It added that the race had been neutralised and the scheduled podium ceremony would not take place as a sign of "respect and mourning".

More to follow.

News.title: Bezos-backed consortium buys a third of Liverpool FC
News.content:
Liverpool's owners have agreed to sell around a third of the club to a consortium including billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

In a statement, Fenway Sports Group (FSG) confirmed it had entered into a "definitive agreement" for the sale of a "strategic minority investment" to 1892 Holdings.

The group is led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia and also includes billionaire Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

Bhatia is set to become Liverpool's vice-chairman, and will join an expanded board pending regulatory approval.

The son-in-law of Indian billionaire businessman Lakshmi Mittal, he had been a director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers for 18 years before relinquishing his stake in the club last month.

American businessman Bezos, founder of e-commerce giant Amazon, is the fourth-richest person in the world, with an estimated net worth of $256bn (Â£192bn). This marks his first foray into sports ownership, although he will not join Liverpool's board.

However, Bryan Baum, founder of venture capital firm K5 Sports - through which Bezos is investing - will join the Anfield board, alongside Saverin's wife Elaine.

BBC Sport has been told that the transaction will have no impact on the club's approach to the transfer window, and that there is no new or separate transfer budget associated with the investment.

The deal is said to value the club between Â£5bn and Â£6bn.

News.title: Prisoners charged over attack on Sara Sharif's father
News.content:
Two prisoners have been charged with the attempted murder of fellow inmate Urfan Sharif who was jailed for killing his daughter Sara Sharif.

Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, have also been charged with other offences relating to the incident in Belmarsh Prison on 1 January 2025, the Crown Prosecution Service said.

The men will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court for a first hearing on 26 August.

Sharif, 43, and Sara's stepmother Beinash Batool were sentenced to life imprisonment after being convicted at the Old Bailey for murdering 10-year-old Sara at their home in Woking, Surrey.

Sharif reportedly suffered cuts to his face during the attack, and received medical treatment at the prison.

Daren Streeter, deputy chief crown prosecutor at CPS London, said: "Our prosecutors have worked closely with the Metropolitan Police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court and pursue criminal proceedings."

Sara was hooded, burned and beaten during a "campaign of torture" that lasted two years before her body was found at the family home in August 2023.

During the trial, Justice Cavanagh told the court "the degree of cruelty involved is almost inconceivable".

Urfan Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison for murder, while his wife Beinash Batool, 30, received a minimum of 33 years.

Sara's uncle, Faisal Malik, 29, was sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment for causing or allowing her death.

The three fled to Islamabad, Pakistan, with Sara's five siblings, the day before her body was found, prompting an international manhunt.

They hid out there for four weeks before returning to the UK, where they were arrested.

News.title: Glastonbury festival organiser dismisses rumours that Madonna will headline in 2027
News.content:
Glastonbury organiser Emily Eavis has said the festival has booked its headliners for next summer - but scotched rumours that Madonna will be among them.

Asked about the 2027 line-up and the speculation that the Queen of Pop would make her Glastonbury debut, Eavis told Katie Razzall on BBC Radio 4's PM programme: "No, it's definitely not Madonna, I'll tell you that.

"But we have got three [other] headliners and we're very excited about it - it's all coming together really well," Eavis added.

And when asked about the possibility of a performance from Taylor Swift, Eavis laughed and said she didn't want to discuss the line-up any more.

News.title: Watch: Moment €9m worth of art stolen from Italy museum
News.content:
Police have recovered three paintings that were stolen from a museum in Italy earlier this year.

CCTV footage of the theft on the night of 22 March was released by authorities, showing two masked thieves breaking into the Magnani Rocca Museum, near the city of Parma.

It is estimated the paintings have a combined worth of â¬9m (Â£7.8m), making it one of the most significant art thefts in Italy in recent years.

Police confirmed in a statement that the paintings by CÃ©zanne, Renoir, and Matisse were recovered during searches, but gave no further details.

The investigation is continuing.

News.title: 'Glam helps mentality' says sprinter Amy Hunt, but can it give you that winning edge?
News.content:
They say practice makes perfect, but for some athletes that means more than just training to be as fast as possible.

For many, it's also about what you wear or how you accessorise with things like jewellery.

So can getting glammed up help your performance?

British sprinter Amy Hunt certainly thinks so, and it seems to be working as she's now secured two gold medals at the European Athletics Championships.

The 24-year-old, who's gunning for a historic quadruple win at the event this week, told BBC Newsbeat "the glam definitely helps that mentality because sprinting is such a confidence game".

"Everyone knows I love a bit of glam and I love my nails."

The Midlands-born athlete has curated her nail art to reference landmarks within Birmingham, where the competition is being held, including nods to the Jewellery Quarter and the Bull Ring, external.

Hunt says "looking good and feeling good" is all part of her process to get into the right mindset, and likens walking out on to the track to a gladiator entering an arena.

"It's a show at the end of the day," she says.

Fellow athletes, including Olympic champions Keely Hodgkinson and the United States' Sha'Carri Richardson and Noah Lyles, are among those who have also become known for their statement nail art on the field, but it's by no means a new practice.

US Olympic champion track star Florence Griffith Joyner, known as Flo-Jo, is often regarded as a pioneer of competing with long, vibrant nails back in the 1980s.

News.title: Mother jailed for killing baby by burning her with a hairdryer
News.content:
A mother who killed her baby daughter by burning her with a hairdryer has been jailed for six years.

Courtney Gartshore, 28, used the appliance to subject three-month-old Dahlia-Rose to "significant and sustained heat" on her head and body.

Emergency services were called to the scene at a property in Peterhead, Aberdeenshire, in September 2023, but the child had died.

Gartshore was convicted of culpable homicide - the closest equivalent to manslaughter in Scots Law - following a trial at the High Court in Aberdeen in July.

Warning: This article contains details readers may find upsetting

Sentencing Gartshore at the High Court in Edinburgh, judge Simon Collins KC told her, external she had inflicted "severe and disfiguring" burns on her daughter.

He said: "Given Dahlia-Rose's very young age, and the horrifying way that she died, this is a uniquely disturbing and distressing case.

"But it is tragic as well as terrible. And that is because the evidence suggested that the accused loved Dahlia-Rose, yet will have to live the rest of her life with the knowledge that she was responsible for her death."

News.title: Woman cleared of owning XL bully which fatally bit man
News.content:
A woman has been cleared of owning an XL bully dog that bit her partner's father, causing him to bleed to death.

Chanel Fong, 33, was accused of owning the dog, Cookie, which was dangerously out of control and of an alternative charge of being the person in charge of the animal at the time of the attack.

She was found not guilty of both by the jury at Caernarfon Crown Court.

Her partner's father, Keven Jones, 62, from Chester, died from severe blood loss after being bitten on the leg.

The attack took place before XL Bullies were added to the banned dog list.

The court heard Keven Jones had been in poor health and had been taking methadone and blood thinning medication, and had been staying at Fong's Wrexham home in May 2022.

Fong said the dog belonged to her partner Joshua Jones, who was not present when his father was bitten, although the prosecution claimed she was Cookie's joint owner.

The court was told there had been a number of dogs at the home on Holt Road in Wrexham, including two XL Bullies, called Fire and Rogue.

Rogue was Cookie's mother and in season at the time, so had to be kept separate from other dogs.

At about 11:30 BST on 23 May, Jones told Fong he would get Cookie and another dog in from the garden, but he was then heard shouting at Cookie to "get off" him.

The court heard Fong also called into the garden for Cookie to get down, which is when Jones came towards her "wobbly".

He pointed to his leg, which was pumping blood, and he said to Fong, "he's got me there".

Fong called the emergency services and attempted first aid, including applying pressure to the wound, but Jones could not be saved.

A post-mortem examination said he had died from extreme blood loss caused by dog bites.

Cookie was later humanely euthanised.

News.title: Sign of life as bright orange 'fire fungus' grows at park ravaged by wildfire
News.content:
A fungus that grows in places damaged by fire has been found at the site of a major wildfire in the Cairngorms National Park.

Forestry and Land Scotland (FLS) said the bright orange, pyrophilous (fire-loving) fungus could be the first sign of nature's recovery at Glenmore near Aviemore.

A wildfire started in the area on 15 July and the incident, which has burned through thousands of acres of woodland and moor, continues to be monitored for hotspots.

FLS said the fungus was among the "first colonisers" of burned ground and played a role in breaking down carbon and preventing soil erosion.

News.title: One million sign petition to keep PC Harper's killers in jail
News.content:
A petition to block the early release of PC Andrew Harper's killers has been signed by more than one million people.

The police officer, from Wallingford, Oxfordshire, died in 2019 when he was dragged by a car as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers were sentenced to 13 years for his manslaughter in 2020 but could be released next year under plans to tackle prison overcrowding. The prime minister is looking at ways to keep them in jail.

Thames Valley Police (TVP) Federation acknowledged the important milestone the petition had reached "without fanfare" due to the seventh anniversary of the officer's death on Saturday.

The petition was started by TVP federation chair Aileen O'Connor who said the decision to consider the killers for early release "pours salt into wounds that have never healed".

She added it was an "insult to Andrew's family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family".

The federation thanked all those who have signed in support.

News.title: Disability campaigners call for Burnham to delay assisted dying bill
News.content:
Disabled and terminally ill campaigners have written to Prime Minister Andy Burnham urging him to reform social and palliative care before assisted dying legislation is introduced in England and Wales.

The Assist Us To Live group says people are currently being "failed by society" and "introducing assisted dying in these circumstances will put sick and disabled people's lives at risk".

Burnham believes the funding of palliative and social care should be "fixed" before assisted dying is considered. The government is likely to remain officially neutral, but the PM's remarks suggest he personally will not back the bill proposed by Labour MP Lauren Edwards.

Bill supporters argue improving care services and giving terminally ill people "autonomy" over their final weeks must go hand in hand.

The proposed law - known as the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - would allow people over the age of 18 who were expected to die within six months to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.

Having a disability in and of itself does not mean you would be able to seek help to end your life.

This is the second time a backbench bill like this is going through the House of Commons.

MPs voted in favour of a bill proposed by Labour MP Kim Leadbetter in 2025, but it was not passed by the House of Lords after an unprecedented number of suggested amendments delayed its progress until it ran out of time in April this year.

Edwards reintroduced an identical bill in June in order to "finish the job" started by Leadbeater. It is due to be debated in the Commons on 11 September.

Opponents of the bill believe the legislation has substantial flaws and would pose risks to disabled people, putting pressure on them to end their lives.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission, the UK's regulator, says legislation is "likely to have particular impacts on people with certain protected characteristics, especially older and disabled people, external".

Last year, the commission's chair Baroness Falkner said: "While the bill provides safeguards against a person being coerced or pressured to end their own life by another individual, we know that disabled people, older people and especially older disabled people, may feel pressured to prematurely end their lives by societal attitudes and a lack of the support and services they need."

Edwards has said there is time to improve end-of-life care before any assisted dying service would come into effect under her proposed law, given a four-year implementation period had been agreed in the previous debates.

News.title: NHS service admits data breach due to pager use
News.content:
The sensitive medical data of transplant patients from across the UK was routinely sent over an unencrypted pager network, an NHS service has admitted.

A BBC investigation found NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) sent the names, dates of birth and types of organs being offered or needed to members of hospital transplant teams who were using pagers, unaware they were not encrypted.

In 2019, then-Health Secretary Matt Hancock announced the NHS in England should stop using pagers by 2021, but some parts of the organisation have continued doing so.

NHSBT said it was "deeply sorry" and has reported the data breach to the Information Commissioner. It added it has now stopped sending patient data in this way.

Pagers are small battery operated radio receivers - popular in the 1980s and 1990s - that can receive short text messages, numbers to call, or alerts.

They are a one-way communication system and only able to receive messages, not send them, which was why they largely fell out of public use as more and more people started carrying mobile phones.

News.title: Man died after being 'trampled' by cattle on estate
News.content:
A man injured in the grounds of a National Trust estate died from "severe chest injuries" after being trampled by cattle, an inquest has heard.

John Orton, 78, a retired telecommunications engineer, died at Felbrigg Hall, near Cromer in Norfolk on 13 July.

Assistant coroner for Norfolk, Maeve Sykes, opened an inquest into his death at Norfolk Coroner's Court on Friday and said a post-mortem examination gave a provisional cause of death as "severe chest injuries".

A National Trust spokesperson said: "We have been left shocked and deeply saddened by the death of a visitor who was seriously injured while walking at Felbrigg last month."

On 13 July, Norfolk Police were called to the estate at about 11:45 BST and said despite efforts to save him, Orton died at the scene.

Following the incident, the estate was closed while inquiries were carried out.

News.title: Final day of heatwave for many before weekend cooldown
News.content:
Kew Gardens in London reached 38.1C on Thursday, making it the UK's hottest day of 2026 so far, and the fifth hottest UK day on record.

It is also the second time this year that the temperature has reached 38C, after Lingwood, Norfolk recorded 38.0C on 26 June.

This is only the second time that 38C has been reached twice in the same year - the previous occasion being 2022.

Though the Met Office amber warning for extreme heat that covered large swathes of England on Thursday expired at midnight, high temperatures will linger in central and eastern parts of England on Friday.

Long spells of sunshine will lift temperatures to 29-34C (84-93F) across large parts of the Midlands, Lincolnshire, East Anglia and the south-east.

For many places it will mark a third consecutive day above official heatwave thresholds.

The heat will ease elsewhere.

Somewhat cooler conditions will begin to move into northern and western parts of the UK, although temperatures will generally remain above the norm for the time of year - widely reaching the low to mid-20s Celsius.

Many places will be dry with a mix of cloud and sunny spells although a few showers are possible, and these could be heavy and thundery in some places.

News.title: Best beauty advent calendars for 2026, reviewed as they drop
News.content:
When do beauty advent calendars usually launch?

In previous years, Liberty has kicked off the advent proceedings at the end of July, with most retailers and brands following suit into August and September. In 2026, however, a glut of beauty advent calendars dropped in July, including Harrods, Lush, Tatcha and Fortnum and Mason. The majority of other advents were subsequently revealed – in one way or another, with some brands still holding exact product rosters close to their chests – through the first week of August. As it stands, only Selfridges is left among the big four London department stores (together with Harvey Nichols , Harrods and Liberty ) to unveil its 2026 Christmas countdown.

Are beauty advent calendars worth it?

In short, yes, beauty advent calendars are always worth more than what you’ll pay; however, you have to consider whether they’ll be worth it for you personally. I’ve been diving into the best beauty advent calendars since 2015 (my first was from M&S) and I can say with confidence that some brands undoubtedly offer a better haul than others. Key things to consider are:

Do you travel a lot – Minis are part and parcel of a beauty advent calendar, so having a place to use them will be key.

Are you unsure where to start in your skincare, haircare or make-up routine – Minis can also be a great way to introduce yourself to premium brands without forking out so much initially

Do you have the time – With everything from face masks to hair bonding treatments within, these products will seriously level up your beauty regimen, but you’ll need to set aside an extra five or ten minutes to use them

What’s your budget – If you’re looking to spend less than £100, you’ll definitely have less big-name brands to choose from your haul. I recommend tallying up the cost of the products you like the look of to ensure you’re getting more than £100 of value from those formulas specifically. Extra products aren’t valuable if you won’t use them.

What is the price range of beauty advent calendars?

Beauty advent calendars can range in price from £40 to £650, with brands such as Revolution (£37.50, Boots.com ) sitting at the lower end, and luxury perfumers like Byredo in the premium price category. More typically, the core beauty advent calendars (from Boots to Harrods ) cost between £100 and £285 – though I’d argue you don’t need to spend more than £250 to take home a seriously spectacular haul.

What is the cheapest beauty advent calendar?

While there are calendars from make-up brands such as W7 (approximately £24) that offer beauty advent calendars below £30, I’d recommend looking to the likes of Revolution (£37.50, Boots.com ), Soap and Glory (£43.20, Boots.com ) and Boots x Macmillan (£44, Boots.com ) for more exciting yet affordable products.

For instance, W7 mimics packaging from Charlotte Tilbury and Estee Lauder products – to name a few – but doesn’t *actually* replicate the formula. However the Boots x Macmillan calendar boasts best-selling brands including Liz Earle and No7. After all, if your calendar costs less but you never use the products within, have you really saved money?

What was the most popular beauty advent calendar last year?

In 2025 the Space NK beauty advent calendar was arguably the most popular and sold out within a few weeks of its September launch. In fact, in previous years it was reported that two Space NK advent calendars sold every minute after its release. Following closely behind the Cult Beauty advent calendar is always a best-seller and, this year, the Harrods fragrance advent calendar has already sold out, so I’m expecting the retailer’s main beauty offering to run out of stock in the coming weeks, too.

Why you can trust IndyBest reviews

As a senior shopping writer, this will be Lucy Smith’s third year reviewing the best beauty advent calendars for IndyBest. Prior to her professional coverage, Lucy has been purchasing beauty advents from M&S, The White Company and more since 2015, putting her experience in the category at more than 10 years. Elsewhere, Lucy covers all the latest beauty launches – such as the Dyson supersonic travel dryer – year round, so she knows what the must-have products of 2026 are for this year’s advent offering. Plus, having reviewed everything from the best foundations to the best hyaluronic acid, she’s well versed in the brands that pop (and the ones that flop), so you can trust that her round-up of the best beauty advent calendars for 2026 isn’t full of hot air.

News.title: WhatsApp update adds AI-powered ‘Scam Alert’ feature that screens messages
News.content:
WhatsApp is adding a new “Scam Alert” feature that checks whether people really are who they claim.

The new tool uses artificial intelligence to check through messages from people who aren’t in a user’s contacts. It looks at “conversational structure and linguistic signals” to try and understand whether a message is likely to be part of a scam.

If WhatsApp thinks that it is, it will show a warning in the chat that will not be visible to the other person. The user can then decide whether to block or report the user sending it – or carry on as normal.

The tool has to be manually switched on. When it is, the app downloads a machine learning model that can check those messages – and is run entirely on the device, meaning that none of the conversation is sent to WhatsApp or to another third party, parent company Meta stressed.

Some information is shared with WhatsApp. To ensure that the feature is working – and to ensure that it stays up to date with new scams – the app gathers particular signals that are confidently processed and are made available entirely anonymously to Meta, it said.

The Scam Alert system is built using previous conversations that WhatsApp users have reported as possible scams. Those conversations are then used to build an AI-powered system that can identify whether a new message is similar, and therefore likely to be illegitimate.

For now, the feature is rolling out in a limited beta version, to early users. The company will “stress-test” the system and has encouraged researchers to try and find bugs within it, before it will be rolled out to all WhatsApp users.

Around 150 people have been evacuated after a fire broke out at a 13-storey hotel in Wembley on Friday (14 July).

Six fire engines and around 40 firefighters rushed to the Holiday Inn in Empire Way just after 12.30pm as London’s emergency services operate under severe pressure during the city’s fifth heatwave this year.

The hotel, believed to house asylum seekers, has been evacuated. No one is believed to have been injured.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) received 29 emergency 999 calls, as the first report of a fire was recorded at 12:34 pm on Empire Way.

Control officers quickly deployed crews from Park Royal, Willesden, Northolt, and surrounding stations to bring the blaze under control.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation. No casualties or injuries have been reported so far.

There is currently no indication any events at Wembley Stadium this weekend will be disrupted by the nearby fire on Empire Way.

The Weeknd is set to play Wembley Stadium tonight as part of his After Hours Til Dawn tour alongside guest performer Playboi Carti, while Ghanaian star Stonebwoy performs at the nearby OVO Arena.

Tens of thousands of concertgoers are expected to arrive in Wembley from Friday evening onwards, placing heightened demand on local transport networks and public safety officers.

The fire at Empire Way comes as the country’s emergency services face unprecedented demand due to the current heatwave the UK is under.

With Thursday having been recorded as the UK’s hottest day this year, prime minister Andy Burnham warned the UK faced “tinder-box conditions”, with a spike in fire and heat-related callouts.

Extreme operational strain continues to build on emergency services nationwide, with Thursday’s devastating wildfire confirmed to have torched 40-acres in Stourbridge.

open image in gallery Blazes in the West Midlands led to thousands of 999 calls, and have caused "extensive" devastation this week ( PA )

The West Midlands Fire Service has described the blaze — which is one of 11 major fires in the region over a 24-hour period — as "one of the most significant" in its history, as 999 control rooms were overwhelmed with thousands of calls.

The Wembley blaze adds to the growing scrutiny on the prime minister, as he faces mounting pressure to tackle the climate emergency.

open image in gallery Environmental groups continue to call on Burnham to address the climate crisis ( Reuters )

Over his premiership, Burnham has faced consistent criticism from environmental campaigners over his hesitation to enact drastic policies against non-renewable energy, and prohibit North sea drilling.

As over half of the country continues to grapple with drought, the London Fire Brigade has urged residents and visitors to exercise caution, stay hydrated, and refrain from activities that could accidentally ignite outdoor fires.
