It's also worth noting that Transfermarkt's valuations only factor contract lengths to a limited extent, meaning the true impact on valuations could be even greater than the data suggests.

What are the biggest factors?

By correlating Premier League player profiles and Transfermarkt transfer values, we found that age and contract runway rank as the two biggest factors in determining player value.

The other contributing factors, according to our analysis, are short and long-term player form, club strength, quantified by Opta's power rankings, and recent availability, measured by minutes played.

Sports.title: Liverpool owners seal £1.65bn sale of 30% stake to consortium that includes Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
Liverpool’s owner, Fenway Sports Group, has confirmed it has agreed the sale of 30% of the club to a consortium including Amit Bhatia, the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and the Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin. The deal is understood to be worth £1.65bn, valuing Liverpool at £5.5bn, and will see Bhatia become the club’s new vice-chair on an expanded board.

Bhatia, the son-in-law of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, initiated and led talks with FSG on behalf of the 1892 Holdings consortium, a reference to Liverpool’s founding year. The former co-owner of Queens Park Rangers has received financial backing from the Mittal Family Trust, the K5 Sports fund, of which Bezos is the lead investor, and EE Capital, the family office of Elaine and Eduardo Saverin.

Elaine Saverin, wife of Eduardo, and Bryan Baum, co-founder and managing partner of K5 Global, will also join the Liverpool board. Bezos is considered a passive investor and will not have a seat on the board.

Despite the involvement of Bezos, the third richest man in the world with $272bn (£201bn), Eduardo Saverin, worth an estimated $33bn and the Mittal family, worth around $17bn, FSG will remain in operational control of Liverpool as well as majority owners. 1892 Holdings’ investment remains subject to regulatory approval, which could take up to 90 days, and will have no impact on Liverpool’s transfer budget or strategy for this summer. There is also no change to the leadership or day-to-day running of Liverpool.

FSG insist the deal is not part of an exit strategy from a club they acquired in 2010 for £300m after the near-ruinous ownership of Tom Hicks and George Gillett. The transaction does not compel FSG to sell more of the club to 1892 at a future date, or include obligations for 1892 to increase their stake, but it does give Bhatia’s consortium options to purchase more of Liverpool should the majority owners eventually decide to sell.

It is the makeup of Bhatia’s consortium, rather than any financial need, that FSG claim attracted them to the British-Indian businessman’s proposal. The FSG leadership team of principal owner John W Henry, chair Tom Werner and president Mike Gordon have spent almost a year getting to know Bhatia and believe the deal will create further opportunities for Liverpool in global business, technology and investment, including in the important markets of India and Asia.

View image in fullscreen The sale will have no impact on Liverpool’s transfer budget or strategy for this summer. Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Gordon, who has resumed a more hands-on role at Liverpool following the departure of Michael Edwards as chief executive of football at FSG, said: “Liverpool has always been built by thinking beyond one season and making decisions with the club’s long-term interests in mind. That approach continues to attract interest from respected investors and business leaders around the world.

“As we considered this opportunity, it became clear that Amit and the consortium shared our long-term philosophy and appreciation for what makes Liverpool special. Their experience and perspective will complement the strong foundation already in place, and we look forward to working together.”

With Premier League and Uefa financial regulations linking a club’s spending to turnover, the new investment will not have an immediate benefit for head coach Andoni Iraola and his Liverpool team. However, the commercial opportunities presented by the involvement of Bezos, Bhatia and Saverin will enable the Anfield club to grow their annual revenue significantly. Liverpool’s annual revenue increased to a record £703m in the year ending May 2025.

Speaking on behalf of 1892 Holdings, Bhatia said: “We are incredibly proud to be investing in Liverpool Football Club and to be doing so alongside FSG. We have the utmost respect and admiration for FSG as owners and for everything they have achieved at Anfield.

“To be welcomed as a partner in a club of this stature is a huge privilege. We are making this investment because we believe deeply in Liverpool and its leadership, and we look forward to supporting the club’s continued success for years to come.”

Bhatia was involved in QPR for almost 19 years and took on numerous roles, from chair of the club to chair of the club’s community trust, until transferring his shareholding in July. He is likely to have a more visible presence at Anfield than fellow members of his consortium or FSG.

Sports.title: Continental clash: where world football stands on Fifa and Infantino – explained
Sports.content:
What’s the situation?

The Oceania Football Confederation’s (OFC) decision to belatedly issue a statement following this week’s executive committee meeting praising Fifa’s “progress achieved over the last decade” means all six continental confederations have finally had their say on the fallout from the World Cup sell-off plan that has split world football, with the votes seeming tied at three apiece on the key issue of whether Gianni Infantino should remain as Fifa president.

Significantly however, the individual member associations will not necessarily follow the lead set by their regional confederations, as New Zealand Football (NZF) quickly illustrated by contradicting the OFC’s position in withdrawing their support for Infantino and calling for an independent review of the sell-off plan.

NZF is the biggest federation in the OFC and has previously benefited from Infantino’s patronage as the co-hosts of the 2023 Women’s World Cup with Australia, which demonstrates how even some former allies are turning on the beleaguered president in an unprecedented situation for the global game.

Who supports Infantino?

While the OFC stopped just short of providing a ringing endorsement for Infantino’s re-election other confederations have been more bullish, with the Confederation of African Football (Caf) and the South American confederation (Conmebol) boldly declaring they want him to stay on for a third full term.

The 56-year-old has also received public declarations of support from individual Fifa member associations, some of whom are tied to the confederations who want him out, most significantly Mexico in Concacaf and Qatar and the United Arab Emirates in the Asian Football Confederation.

Significantly the 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia have yet to declare their hand as the Saudi Football Federation is without a president, with elections taking place this month, and their position could be key in determining how many Asian countries follow the lead of the AFC.

Who opposes him?

Uefa has been the most vocal and vociferous opponents, even threatening to boycott Fifa tournaments if Infantino does not withdraw his candidacy, with the vast majority of their 55 members united behind them. The picture in Asia is less clear cut as outlined above, and it is unclear how many of their 47 members back the AFC leadership.

Concacaf’s 41 members appear more united, although the Grenada Football Association on Friday joined Mexico in declaring their support for Infantino.

Mexico is a special case as they have made clear they want to leave the confederation in any case to join Conmebol to gain more lucrative matches against Brazil and Argentina, but senior figures at Uefa are also convinced that individual African countries can be picked off and persuaded to join the rebels.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

What happens next?

After three weeks of frenetic activity football’s civil war has hardened into a stalemate, which is unlikely to be definitively resolved until next year’s presidential election at Fifa Congress in Rabat in March.

With strong allies in Africa and South America, plus the public support of the US president, Donald Trump, there is no prospect of Infantino resigning or withdrawing his candidacy for re-election so a bitterly fought seven-month campaign lies ahead.

The most immediate pinch-point is next month’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland, which European countries have threatened to boycott, although it is unclear whether any teams will actually withdraw. Despite being on a war footing it is likely that Uefa and Fifa will reach a public truce in the next few weeks that would enable the competition to go ahead.

Beyond that the next deadline is 18 November, when candidates for the Fifa presidency must declare their hand, leaving the Uefa-led alliance with just over three months to find and unite behind an alternative to Infantino.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, is seen as the most likely challenger, but will only stand if he is convinced he can win.

With an electorate of 211 Fifa members the rebels are far from certain they are close enough to getting the 106 votes required to oust Infantino.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 10: Fulham
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 15th (NB: this is not necessarily John Brewin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 11th

Prospects

Marco Silva cutting the cord after five years by the river came as little surprise. If his time at Craven Cottage was successful in re-establishing Fulham as a Premier League club, he rarely concealed his ambitions to manage in European competition. He was frequently explicit in his disappointment that the club’s ownership did not meet him halfway by funding a stronger squad. Silva’s powers of rebadging and replenishing talent will be missed now that he has decamped to Benfica. Under him, Fulham played entertaining football, a collection of ugly ducklings showing their renewed worth for a club that, despite falling short of European qualification, looked upwards rather than downwards at the relegation battle. They were often a pleasure to watch, and ornery opposition for all-comers.

Álvaro Arbeloa is a very different type of appointment, with far less experience than his predecessor in frontline coaching terms, even if he arrives with Real Madrid on his CV. His arrival, though, has opened up a working relationship with the Spanish aristos, Gonzalo García and César Palacios arriving to work with a coach who helped them through the ranks in Madrid. By little coincidence, all three share the same agency as their representatives. There have been links with Endrick and Thiago Pitarch, two further young Real jewels, leading to a sense of Fulham becoming some form of Madrileño nursery, a Santiago Bernabéu on Thames. Should that play out, it would represent another sea change.

Silva preferred to work with hard-bitten pros. A couple of his leading men, Raúl Jiménez and Harry Wilson, have departed. The latter played the best football of his career last season but, like his manager, got a better offer elsewhere, from Leeds. Fulham’s latest approach is to source young players and polish them up. Can they have the same successes as mid-tier peers such as Brentford, Brighton and Bournemouth, where the approach is far more data-driven? Will supporters be looking upwards rather than downwards? A previously enigmatic club just got more enigmatic.

Off-field picture

In May, the club were runners-up at the football business awards, for stadium experience, as the Riverside Stand’s opulent hospitality completed its first full season in service. Fulham need the Riverside to deliver as a revenue stream, as financial results for the 2024-25 season showed a pre-tax loss for the year at £44.5m, and that was lowered by the sale of João Palhinha in July 2024. There has been no such windfall since. The Khan family ownership continues to back the club, its overall investment estimated at about £900m, with staff costs at 117% of turnover. Therein lies the reasoning behind Silva not receiving the backing he desired.

Owner-fan relationship

The most expensive season ticket at Craven Cottage comes in at £3,084 for access to the Riverside’s facilities, the highest in the Premier League. Shahid Khan and his son Tony, the vice-chair and director of football operations, are unpopular among committed supporters for price rises and pandering to tourism. Khan’s boat Kismet was named superyacht of the year in 2025, its main salon inspired by the Palace of Versailles, and can be chartered for more than $3m per week. Though the balance sheets confirm Khan’s outlay in funding a continued Premier League status, fans would prefer he recognised not everyone lives the high life.

The manager

Where Silva had an unremarkable playing career, Arbeloa featured among the elite, a World Cup and Champions League winner. He also had the ear of Florentino Pérez, the perennial Real Madrid president asking him to replace Xabi Alonso mid-season in the 2025-26 campaign. That did not pan out and he took his first job away from Madrid, where he was a well-regarded youth coach, in south-west London. Khan Sr’s comment that Arbeloa “believes in giving young players a chance” is pertinent for Fulham’s change in direction. Crucially, as befitting traditions at Craven Cottage, the new man from Salamanca believes in open, attacking football, offering some continuity from Silva’s reign.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García surges forward during Fulham’s Costa del Sol Trophy match against Málaga. Photograph: Joaquin Corchero/AFP7/Shutterstock

Gonzalo García’s reputation was made by his performances at last summer’s Club World Cup, where he won the tournament’s Golden Boot. Comparisons were made to Raúl, a considerable accolade at the Bernabéu. Goals followed in the Champions League against Juventus and Borussia Dortmund but García eventually lost out to the star system of Vinícius Júnior and Kylian Mbappé. His reputation in Spain is as a hard worker off the ball, necessary for a Premier League player. Last season, Rodrigo Muniz’s injuries meant the old soldier Jiménez shouldered the burden at centre-forward. García is younger and fresher but the hype surrounding his arrival gives him much to live up to.

Stat attack

Fulham had the oldest side in the Premier League last season, which may help explain why they had arguably the least intense press. Marco Silva’s side recorded the fewest high turnovers, which occur when a team recovers the ball to start a new open-play possession sequence in the final 40 metres of the pitch. Real Madrid are hardly known for being a high-pressing side but they comfortably outperformed Fulham on this metric. It will be fascinating to see how Arbeloa approaches this.

Set for a breakthrough

Jonah Kusi-Asare’s arrival last summer from Bayern Munich is further mining of a super-club’s youth department. Bayern inserted a buy-back clause for a player they picked up from AIK. The Sweden Under-21s player has been compared to Alexander Isak, and made seven substitute appearances last season – without scoring – before an initial loan became a permanent move. At 6ft 5in he offers a different profile of striker to García. Hayden Mullins, the former under-21 coach now Newport manager, saw the best of Kusi-Asare last season, the 18-year-old scoring five goals in six matches.

World Cup impact

García made his debut for Spain in a pre-World Cup friendly against Iraq but failed to make the eventual champions’ tournament squad. Antonee Robinson had a fine tournament for the USA until the co-hosts perished in the last 16 at the hands of a Belgium team featuring Timothy Castagne. Luc de Fougerolles, yet to play a Premier League game for Fulham, showed off teenage defensive talents in Canada’s run to the knockouts. To complete a successful quintet – saving the best till last? – Sander Berge had a fine tournament as Norway also reached the quarter-finals.

Sports.title: Arsenal open talks with Bayer Leverkusen over deal for Jarell Quansah
Sports.content:
Arsenal have opened talks with Bayer Leverkusen over a move for Jarell Quansah as they intensify efforts to bring in cover for William Saliba and Jurriën Timber.

The England defender, who left Liverpool last summer for an initial £30m and was part of Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad, has been identified as an ideal replacement for the France and Netherlands defenders, who will miss the start of the new season due to injury. While Quansah’s preferred position is in central defence, he was also deployed at right-back by Tuchel at the World Cup and was sent off in the last-16 victory over Mexico.

It is understood that Leverkusen are reluctant to sell the 23-year-old, who signed a five-year deal when he left Anfield last July, and would want at least €50m (£43m). Arsenal – who saw a bid of £30m for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa rejected earlier in the window – are not thought to want to pay that much but now could test the German club’s resolve by submitting a similar offer. Liverpool had a €70m buyback option on Quansah but that has now expired.

Arsenal are still believed to be interested in Konsa, who also filled in at right-back for England during the World Cup but is better known as a central defender. Villa value the 28-year-old at £60m.

Mikel Arteta said this week that Saliba’s back injury would take “some time to heal” and he was unsure about when he would be available again. Arsenal also have concerns over Timber, who pulled out of the Netherlands squad on the eve of the World Cup after failing to recover from a persistent groin injury that forced him to miss most of the run‑in last season.

“Jurriën is progressing really well,” Arteta said after Arsenal’s friendly defeat by Borussia Dortmund last weekend. “He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now, but it’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.”

Arsenal would still like to sign a new attacker before the end of the window and could allow Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus to depart in order to free up more funds. Galatasaray have offered £38m for Martinelli, although the Brazil forward is not thought to be keen on a move to Turkey. Napoli have shown an interest in Jesus.

Ethan Nwaneri could also be sold, with Milan, Fulham, RB Leipzig and Borussia Dortmund among those who have been linked with the 19-year-old.

The future of Myles Lewis-Skelly is unclear after he was offered to Chelsea and Manchester United this week. Arteta refused to address the rumours after he scored in the friendly against Como – managed by Cesc Fábregas – on Wednesday.

“I’m not going to talk about speculation,” he said. “If there is speculation about our players, it’s a good sign. That means our players attract attention and are doing a good job.”

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca says Manchester City will not meet Chelsea’s deadline for Fernández
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca is expecting a busy end to the transfer window but says Manchester City will not meet Chelsea’s 5pm Friday deadline to sign Enzo Fernández.

Maresca takes charge of City for the first time in a major match on Sunday with the Community Shield against Arsenal in Cardiff but is a long way from finalising the squad he will have for the season. City are closing to signing the 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, while Chelsea’s Fernández, who worked with Maresca at Stamford Bridge, is of interest but would cost £120m. The Blues set a 5pm cut-off point on Friday to reach their valuation or not bother.

“Not today to be honest, I don’t think we’re going to do something today,” Maresca said. “For sure there are things we need to do, how many I don’t know, can be one can be two depends also if players want to leave so we can see. It’s 48 hours for the final, my first final in this club, I would like to win my first trophy, so my focus isn’t on players that can leave or players that can arrive, my focus is on the game.”

The club have rejected two bids from Barcelona for Rodri and are expected to sell Tijjani Reijnders in the coming days.

Rodri, who has a year remaining on his contract, returned to the club on Friday after his holiday following the culmination of a triumphant World Cup but Maresca would not be drawn on the midfielder’s immediate future, with a third Barcelona offer expected.

“The transfer window is open, we can buy players, we can sell players, anything can happen. I just saw Rodri now in the building, I gave him a big hug, he looks good, so we’ll see what happens.”

Reijnders is set to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Qadsiah after the two clubs agreed a £51m fee for the Dutchman, who moved to City last summer from Milan but wants more regular playing time.

“They all work every day, they all do sessions every day and at the end of the week they all want to play a game,” Maresca said. “When they don’t play, they struggle to understand or they struggle to see the reason why and I can understand that after one season some of them would like to play a little bit more. It’s a normal situation.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Rangers and the paradox of a painful exit that boosts their trophy chances
Sports.content:
AND NOW FOR SOME PERSPECTIVE

All new managers want to hit the ground running. But landing with a dull thud has never been a barrier to future glory, certainly not at Ibrox. Take Graeme Souness, whose start as Rangers’ player-manager put the ‘pish’ in ‘inauspicious’. On his league debut, away to Hibs, he was sent off in the first half after a revenge attack on the wrong mullet. Rangers lost 2-1 and were beaten in the third game as well. Graeme out! Rangers won the League Cup and finished the season as champions for the first time in nine years.

Dick Advocaat had a similarly awkward start in 1998. In his first game, played at Tranmere’s Prenton Park, Rangers went 3-0 down to Shelbourne in the first leg of their Big Vase tie. They went through comfortably in the end but lost the first league game a few days later. Dic- Advocaat out! Rangers had to settle for a domestic treble that season. Different times, when toys were played with for more than a few seconds before being launched from the pram with maximum force, followed a few seconds later by a handful of freshly sourced excreta. In 2026, alas, hot air and horse pucky are an acceptable substitute for reasonable discourse. And so, after failing to win any of his first four games as Rangers manager, Derek McInnes is “out of his depth” and a “dead man walking”.

Que Sera, Sera? Eff that! Turns out the future is ours to see after four games, two of them in a competition Rangers had no chance of winning anyway. Football Daily hasn’t a clue if McInnes is up to the Brobdingnagian challenge of managing Rangers, one that most tea-timely newsletters don’t really understand. But we do know that a culture of self-fulfilling poppycock, where ostentatious negativity is football’s version of the fatberg and many people would rather be right than happy, is a stain on our daily bread.

That said, what a roflcopter of a start! Given the events of last season, it was never going to be an equanimity-cultivating experience for a new Rangers manager to see Russell Martin’s start and lower it. Rangers have one point from two league games and are out of Bigger Vase after the most costly 1-1 draw against Polish opposition on British soil since Brian Clough called somebody a clown. Paradoxically, the aggregate defeat to Jagiellonia Bialystok – and subsequent drop into Tin Pot – has increased Rangers’ chances of winning a trophy under McInnes. Time will tell whether those chances have increased from 0.0000001% to 0.0000002%, from 9% to 9.4% or from some other figure to some other figure. Right now, the supercomputers know, and the bairns in the prams certainly don’t.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“If Gianni Infantino doesn’t get re-elected unanimously, then whoever voted against him needs to get their head examined” – Andrew Giuliani, the chief suit of the White House Task Force for the Geopolitics World Cup, emerges from Donald Trump’s fundament to give his view on the Fifa crisis. Sports.title: How will the three promoted teams fare in the Premier League?
Sports.content:
Coventry

A quarter of a century after their last appearance in the Premier League – following financial ruin, ground-sharing in Northampton and Birmingham and even a spell in League Two – Coventry have finally completed their comeback story. But the bunting has been packed away and they now face the daunting task of proving they belong in the top flight.

Frank Lampard is not starting from scratch. Coventry’s success last season was a collective effort and a product of smart recruitment over the past few years. The result was a side that overwhelmed the Championship with a fearless front-footed approach without relying on a single scorer. Seven Coventry players scored seven or more league goals.

They led the division for shots on target; they ranked second for big chances created, touches in the opposition’s final third and touches in the penalty area; and they produced direct attacking speed and passes-per-sequence numbers comparable to those of some of the Premier League’s most direct sides, including Brentford and Bournemouth.

The title was wrapped up with three games to spare; they conceded the fewest goals in the division (45 in 46 games); and their 97-goal haul was the fourth highest in a 46-game Championship season, behind only Fulham in 2021–22, Bournemouth in 2014–15 and Reading in 2005–06. Given the success Fulham and Bournemouth have enjoyed in recent years, Coventry will hope that proves a good omen.

Continuity is going to be central to their hopes of survival. They are not following in the footsteps of Sunderland, who spent about £155m last summer. Coventry’s net spend was about £3.5m last summer and just 17% of minutes on the pitch last season went to newcomers. Their best business in the transfer window was holding on to players such as Jack Rudoni and Milan van Ewijk, who were attracting interest from top-flight clubs.

View image in fullscreen Coventry’s captain, Matt Grimes, and manager, Frank Lampard enjoy the Championship parade. Now comes the hard part. Photograph: Hannah McKay/Reuters

They have not gone wild this summer but they have invested. Coventry have signed the centre-back Aurèle Amenda from Eintracht Frankfurt, the winger Loum Tchaouna from Burnley, and the midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi from Nordsjælland while also securing permanent deals for Frank Onyeka and Carl Rushworth, who were on loan at the club last season. They have also brought back the former favourite Gustavo Hamer after his spell at Sheffield United.

Lampard’s biggest challenge will be adapting a style built to dominate in the Championship into one capable of surviving the Premier League. Their direct, attacking approach will be riskier against opponents who possess the pace, quality and tactical sophistication to punish a rushed pass or a risky vertical ball.

Coventry will not have the same territorial control or volume of chances they enjoyed last season either – they need players who can get them up the pitch. Haji Wright’s pace and ability to attack space should be valuable, but Ellis Simms, who tends to thrive attacking the penalty area, will need service.

Hull

The fact Hull are playing in the Premier League this season borders on miraculous. This is a side that survived relegation to League One on goal difference the season before last, entered 2025-26 under a transfer embargo, scraped into the playoffs by beating Norwich on the final day of the season, and scored a stoppage-time winner in the playoff final. No one backed them in their pre-season predictions and yet, under the guidance of the relatively unknown Sergej Jakirovic in his first season in charge, they defied the statistics.

If matches in the Championship last season had been decided by expected goals, Hull would have finished second bottom. The glaringly obvious problem was at the back. They conceded 66 goals, giving them the fourth worst defensive record in the Championship. Looking back at the last 15 teams to be promoted to the Premier League, only Southampton (who conceded 63 goals when they were promoted in 2023-24) have come close to that tally and they went on to concede 86 goals in the top flight, finishing rock bottom with just 12 points.

As if that weren’t bad enough, Hull were lucky to not concede more: opponents failed to convert 10 opportunities where they had at least a 50% chance of scoring according to xG – the most of any side in the league. Hull simply have to improve as fortune does not tend to stick around long when you’re in the Premier League.

There are some reasons for optimism, though. Their form against the top teams in away matches was impressive. They conceded just eight goals in their matches at the teams in the top 10; they did not concede in either of their games against Coventry; and they didn’t concede in any of their playoff matches.

View image in fullscreen Hull City players celebrate reaching the Premier League with a victory parade. Photograph: Bruce Rollinson/PA

Jakirovic showed an impressive knack of switching tactics depending on whom his side faced or how a game was evolving. His switch from their usual 4-2-3-1 formation to a back three with wingbacks in the second leg of their playoff tie against Millwall was perhaps the most telling example of this succeeding as they caught Millwall by surprise, winning 2-0 at the Den. If continuity is the key word in Coventry’s fight for survival then chaos seems to be Hull’s. You don’t really know what to expect from them. The striker Oli McBurnie pointed this out last season: “It’s probably hard to gameplan against us, because we play so many different ways against different teams.”

As well as their unpredictability, this team have heart. They defied all expectations to reach the top, overcoming a relegation battle, a transfer embargo and statistical odds. Jakirovic put their success down to the bond they have forged. “It was like a puzzle,” he said. “Maybe it was the best that it happened like this. This group of players became even closer. They had to stick together and help each other.” As Robert Earnshaw, who played for Derby in their disastrous 2007-08 campaign, has warned: “You can relegate yourself based on how you think. It was almost as if everyone gave up. It was 20 games to go and it was like: ‘We’re never going to do it.’” This Hull side have fight and that should count for something.

Ipswich

Two years ago Ipswich entered the Premier League as one of football’s feelgood stories. After they had had 22 years away from the top flight, Kieran McKenna took them back through back-to-back promotions, turning a squad largely built for League One into Championship contenders. The 2023-24 campaign was fuelled by fearless, attacking football, late goals and a sense of togetherness, with Ipswich finishing second behind Leicester and becoming the first side in 12 years to climb from League One to the Premier League in successive seasons.

McKenna’s side had an established core who had grown together and exceeded expectations but they were small fish in a very big pond, and the Premier League quickly exposed the gulf in quality. Ipswich won just four games, conceded 82 times and finished 19th with 22 points. Their immediate return to the top flight, fuelled by Premier League experience and parachute payments, means this is a very different promotion story – less about underdogs defying expectations and more about a club that is aiming to belong in this league.

Their recruitment in 2024 suggested they had one eye on a return to the second tier. They brought in leading Championship players who had potential but were not proven at the top: Omari Hutchinson, Jack Clarke, Liam Delap, Dara O’Shea and Jacob Greaves. The club’s CEO, Mark Ashton, says they have to be “a bit braver” this time around. Rather than focusing on potential, they want to sign battle-ready, established top-flight performers.

Florentino Luís and Sasa Lukic bring the physicality and ball-winning presence the midfield lacked in 2024-25, while Issa Diop adds Premier League experience at the back. At the other end, with no Ipswich player scoring more than 10 non-penalty goals last season, Emersonn gives them a physically imposing striker, while Daizen Maeda and Abdul Fatawu add running power and intensity. Crucially, a lot of these players have Premier League experience and, with O’Shea, Clarke, Greaves and Jaden Philogene remaining from the season they went down, this is a side that look more ambitious and ready to compete.

Their defence also looks far more equipped for the top flight. They had the second best defensive record in the Championship last season, keeping 17 clean sheets and conceding just 47 goals (10 fewer goals than when they were promoted in 2023-24). This is not the chaotic and entertaining side that got them to the Premier League two years ago, but a more patient team that know how to be pragmatic and aggressive.

The biggest negative is the departure of the man who guided them back to the Premier League, with McKenna stepping away from football. Gary O’Neil, his replacement, has experienced Premier League relegation battles with Bournemouth and Wolves but it will be difficult to replace the identity, relationships and collective belief McKenna spent five years building through three promotions in four years, and 105 wins in 222 games. O’Neil is inheriting a more expensive and talented side than Ipswich had two years ago, but he will have to hit the ground running and help a host of new players to adapt quickly.

This is an article by WhoScored

Sports.title: Lincoln trust in double act as second-tier return starts at Middlesbrough
Sports.content:
The last thing the Championship needs is another spying scandal, so when a lorry emblazoned with KGB parked up alongside Lincoln City’s training ground on Tuesday lunchtime there was laughter as staff pondered whether the Soviet Union was examining their set pieces. It shows the relaxed atmosphere at one of the second tier’s newest clubs, one that has had a summer of change yet maintained continuity by appointing joint head coaches.

Tom Shaw and Chris Cohen have replaced Michael Skubala, who led the Imps to 103 points and promotion back to this level after 65 years away before leaving for Bristol City. It was a symbiotic appointment because while the former assistants were devising a sales pitch to the club’s hierarchy, the wheels were already in motion to promote from within. Their plan is to banish English football’s memories of Liverpool’s ill-fated pairing of Roy Evans and Gérard Houllier. The duo are doing final preparations for Saturday’s season opener at the Riverside against Middlesbrough, who have spent more than £20m on summer signings – Lincoln have spent a quarter of that across their 142-year history, indicating the task ahead.

“The difference is that they’re put together by a football club, Evans and Houllier being the prime example, it’s two men just put together and told to go and do the same job,” says Cohen in the office he shares with Shaw. “Me and Tom have formed a relationship over the last few years where the club has seen our relationship as a pair of coaches and blokes evolve. We drive in together, we drive home together, we spend all of our days together, when we’re off, we’ll have a game of golf together.

“They understand that if it is going to work with any two coaches, then this is probably the one with the best chance because we see football the same way, we see life the same way, we see our principles are very, very similar. We obviously have differences in small decisions and nuances within everything, but principally we see the way that a football club should be run and the team should play very, very similarly. That gives us a really good chance.”

Lincoln are a forward-thinking club but the latest major decision is not about experimentation. The duo fit the club’s philosophy, having worked within academies giving them the skills to develop players, as they did with Jack Moylan, who was sold to Cardiff for a record fee. Shaw and Cohen were key members of Skubala’s staff, taking on great responsibility, and Lincoln were keen to reward their progression and give the squad continuity. The players have been told not to call them “gaffer or boss”.

They complement one another, with Cohen’s focus on the defence and Shaw the attack to share the workload. The pair are rarely side-by-side on the training ground, as they seek different perspectives, whether watching a session taken by the other head coach or the former Hull defender Paul McShane, while David Preece oversees goalkeeping.

“We do get to the end of some days and we look at each other and go: ‘Thank God we’ve got each other,’” says Cohen. “Thank God there’s two of us to do that, what we’ve just created on that day on the training pitch or gameplans. I’ve been an assistant for a long time, so I’ve had that relationship with managers where I’ve had their full trust, but there is a different feel about having the final decision and being sure that you’re making the right one. To have two of us to check and challenge each other and then come out with hopefully the best logical decision for the team.” The bickering, they say, is left for golf.

View image in fullscreen Lincoln’s analysts preparing data after a training session. Photograph: Gary Calton/The Guardian

The club have handed out 14 new contracts since promotion, in addition to two permanent signings and three loans to maintain momentum. The 2016-17 run to the FA Cup quarter-finals as a National League side brought prize money which was invested in a purpose-built training ground, having not had one before, which sits between a former RAF base and a potato field. Promotion to the Championship means more income, allowing a £9m upgrade of the ground and training site, with further expansion planned.

One of the few things the pair do apart is holiday, which is when they found out they would be taking over, with Shaw in Greece and Cohen in Spain. Shaw says: “The first two or three days of our holidays were very hectic. We signed the paperwork and then enjoyed the last few days in the swimming pool. There was some emotion in our families,” he adds, looking at a photo of Cohen and him celebrating promotion with their children. “It was just a really nice moment in our journeys and our families know each other and really get on. So just really nice for us to be doing this together and a big moment in our careers.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visit to Sincil Bank has been jokingly used to illustrate the impact of relegation on West Ham but Lincoln are far more than a punchline. They are in the Championship on merit, despite being the bookmakers’ favourites to go down. A deserved 2-1 away win over their divisional rivals Derby in the Carabao Cup last weekend further proved their credentials.

Cohen says: “We hope we’re underestimated, we hope the big clubs in the division when they turn up at Sincil Bank underestimate how good our players are, how good our fans are, how good our stadium is to come to. We’re hoping that clubs take us for granted or underestimate us because it just goes back to that group of players in there that we back to the absolute hilt.

“We’re bringing a couple more recruits hopefully to help with the volume of the squad but as I said all along they’re an amazing group – amazing technically, tactically – but the thing they’ve got is heart and passion which wins you games of football.”

The Riverside will be a key test of their credentials. Shaw says: “We will check and challenge each other through the week. We’ll have minor disagreements throughout the week to get to what we think is the right plan. And then by Thursday, Friday we’re super aligned and massively behind whatever decisions we’ve come to, with the support of all the people as well.”

Sports.title: Aaron Ramsey confirms son of England World Cup star is joining Championship club – but can’t sign until January
Sports.content:
Aaron Ramsey confirms son of England World Cup star is joining Championship club – but can’t sign until January

Oxford United manager Aaron Ramsey has revealed that defender Stan Mills is leaving the club... in January.

Five months before Mills will leave, Ramsey confirmed a deal has been agreed with Preston North End for him to depart.



3 Mills has been confirmed to be leaving Oxford, but not for a few months Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The winger is the son of ex-England international Danny Mills, who made five World Cup appearances for the Three Lions.

He came through Everton's academy from 2018 until 2022, going on to sign for Oxford on loan a year later.

Mills spent a season with the U's before joining permanently at the start of last year, going on to play 43 times in the Championship last term and being named the club's Player of the Season.



However, after the club were relegated to League One, the 22-year-old's future was thrown into doubt.

Preston have had eyes on Mills this summer and they have got their man - but they're going to have to wait for him.



Oxford are currently blocked from making any signings after being placed under a transfer embargo in July, just two weeks after former Arsenal midfielder Ramsey was appointed manager.

And due to that, the U's have made a decision not to sell players either, to make sure their squad doesn't get picked apart.



So, Preston appear to have reached a compromise with their former Championship rivals, agreeing on a transfer for the future.

What has Ramsey said about Mills?

Ramsey revealed in a press conference ahead of his first game as a manager against MK Dons on Saturday: “Stan has agreed a deal to go to Preston in January and, listen, it’s far from ideal, I can totally understand that, one day before the beginning of the season.

“What it does mean is we get Stan now for the next four, five months and then when January comes around, we’ll be in a completely different position where we can be really aggressive in the market and we’ll have to strengthen our squad."

3 Ramsey has admitted that the club can't let any players leave while under embargo Credit: Getty



“The statement has been pretty clear, that we’re retaining our squad," Ramsey explained on Oxford's stance.

"We’re going to need every single one of them, with the situation we’re in and we can’t bring anybody in.

"So, yeah, we’re going to need everybody available for that.”

Keeping quiet

Ramsey's honest admission comes after Preston manager Paul Heckingbottom refused to give anything away regarding Mills.

Heckingbottom said: "He's not our player. I don't talk about other clubs' players. He's not our player, that's it.



"I think if you asked me about him, I'd be comfortable speaking to you about him off record in terms of what I think of him as a lad and a player and what I see from him, but no, not our player, nothing there."

3 Mills was Oxford's POTY last season and Preston have agreed to sign him Credit: PA

"Will he be with us before the end of the window in terms of us being able to do a deal with him? I wouldn't know until there's anything to say, it's pointless speaking."

Since those comments from the Preston boss, it seems a deal has been done with Mills, but with the future in mind.



It means the forward is available for Oxford against MK Dons on Saturday, rather than for Preston against Bolton.

The Lilywhites' clash with Bolton kicks off at 12:30pm, with talkSPORT having exclusive live coverage of the game.

Commentary will be coming from Adam Bridge and former England defender Micky Gray.

Sports.title: Chelsea co-owner keen on selling stake amid investigation from US prosecutors
Sports.content:
Chelsea co-owner keen on selling stake amid investigation from US prosecutors

Chelsea co-owner Mark Walter is reportedly looking to offload his share in the club.

Walter boasts a 12.8 per cent in BlueCo, who are the owners of the Premier League heavyweights.

2 Walter could soon land a hefty boost to his bank balance Credit: Getty

However, according to the Wall Street Journal, the 66-year-old is seeking a way out.

News of Walter's interest in selling his Chelsea stake comes shortly after he sold NBA powerhouse Los Angeles Lakers for an eye-watering $12.5billion [£9.2bn] to Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger.

The staggering sum represents the highest price that has ever been paid for a sports team.

What made Walter's sale of the Lakers all the more intriguing was the fact he purchased the franchise only a year earlier for a then-record $10bn [£7.4bn].

Why is Mark Walter under investigation by US prosecutors?

Walter's withdrawal from the Lakers and potentially Chelsea comes amid an investigation from the U.S. Attorney's Office into potential financial misconduct at two of his insurance companies as well as Guggenheim Partners, which he leads.

The 66-year-old's mobile phone and computer were seized by federal agents aboard a private plane at Midway International Airport in Chicago last September as part of a court-authorised search warrant.

"Mark Walter and TWG have always acted in good faith, and those who have done business with Mark know him as honest and straightforward," TWG Global, Walter's conglomerate, said in a previous statement.

"We are cooperating with authorities, and we are confident these matters will be resolved favorably."

No individuals have been criminally charged as part of the FBI's investigation into the financial improprieties.

Walter is listed as a director on Chelsea's board but his role does not entail day-to-day operations.

2 Todd Boehly is listed as Chelsea's chairman Credit: PA

When did BlueCo take over Chelsea?

BlueCo purchased Chelsea from Roman Abramovich in May 2022 for £4.25bn.

Abramovich was forced to sell after the UK government placed sanctions on him following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

As a result of the sanctions, Abramovich saw none of the proceeds from the sale.

BlueCo have since sunk billions into the club, especially when it comes to transfers.

The latest example of Chelsea breaking the bank for a new player was for Morgan Rogers, who moved from Aston Villa earlier this summer for £117m.

Despite the hefty spending, Chelsea only have two trophies to show for their troubles: the Club World Cup and the Conference League.

Additionally, the Blues have finished inside the top four just once in the last four seasons.

Sports.title: Arsenal identify alternative defender if Jarell Quansah and Ezri Konsa bids fail
Sports.content:
Arsenal have identified Como's Jacobo Ramon should they fail to sign Ezri Konsa or Jarell Quansah, talkSPORT understands.

The Gunners are looking to bring in a new versatile defender this summer, with England pair Konsa and Quansah their main targets.



6 Jacobo Ramon enjoyed a breakthrough season in senior football in 2025/26 after joining Como last summer

The Premier League champions first set their sights on Aston Villa's Konsa, but have so far failed in their efforts to bring him to north London.

Arsenal have already made a verbal offer to Villa for Konsa in the region of £35million, which fell well below his valuation of up to £65m

They have since turned their attention to Bayer Leverkusen's Quansah, holding discussions with the 23-year-old.



The England international only moved to the Bundesliga side from Liverpool last summer, and like Villa, Leverkusen are reluctant to sell one of their prized assets.

Quansah is also unlikely to come cheap - Leverkusen would want to make a profit on the £35m they paid for him, while the defender had a £70m buyback clause which the Reds opted not to trigger.



Plan C

Should Arsenal fail to make a breakthrough in their pursuit of either Konsa or Quansah, they could then look at Como's Ramon.

The 21-year-old joined Cesc Fabregas' side from Real Madrid last summer and made 32 league appearances in the 2025/26 campaign as his team qualified for the Champions League.



Any move for Ramon would benefit his old team, with Real retaining a 50 per cent sell-on clause and a number of buy-back clauses.

Konsa stumbling block explained

Arsenal's pursuit of Ramon hinges on their success in landing either of their top targets, with talkSPORT's Chief Football Correspondent Alex Crook shedding light on this on the latest episode of The Window.

Crook revealed that, despite the Gunners falling short of Konsa's valuation, the Villa defender is keen on a move to the Emirates.

6 Arsenal are set to launch a fresh approach for Konsa, who Villa value at over £60million Credit: Getty



6 Quansah was named in England's World Cup squad after featuring 43 times for Leverkusen last term Credit: Getty

He told talkSPORT: "The Gunners, we're told, are stepping up their pursuit of Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa.

“At the moment, they're quite a way short of Villa's valuation, which we understand to be around £60million.

“But key to this deal, Konsa, we're told, would like to make the move to north London. He'd like to link up with the Premier League champions.



“So, we'll see if Arsenal can get anywhere near Aston Villa's asking price, but this is one that I think definitely could develop over the next few days.

“Mikel Arteta likes Konsa's versatility. He can be a straight swap for [William] Saliba alongside Gabriel at the heart of the champions' defense. He can also play at right back and that's been a problematic area as well - Ben White obviously had his injury issues last season.

“Jurrien Timber is out of this weekend's Community Shield - live on talkSPORT. So, if they can get Konsa because he can play in a multitude of positions, I think it could be a really sensible deal for Arsenal.”

6 Mikel Arteta is keen to sign a new centre-back amid Arsenal's injury issues Credit: Getty



Who else could Arsenal sign?

As well as being keen to strengthen their backline, Arsenal are looking to bolster their left-wing before the end of the transfer window.

Greek winger Christos Tzolis has joined to replace Leandro Trossard, who signed for Besiktas.

Gabriel Martinelli could follow the Belgian to Turkey amidst reports that Galatasaray are interested in the Brazilian wideman, with potential for Victor Osimhen to move in the opposite direction.

But after missing out on a blockbuster move for Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior, the Gunners are still looking for a big-name arrival.



And Crook revealed Juventus star Kenan Yildiz has emerged as a possible summer target for Arsenal, who will need to replace Martinelli should he join Galatasaray.

Explaining who else the Gunners could sign, he explained: "Kenan Yildiz at Juventus has emerged as a possible target."

6 Kenan Yildiz scored 10 goals in 36 Serie A appearances last term Credit: Getty

6 Victor Osimhen could also finally be about to get a move to the Premier League Credit: Getty



As for their other options, Crook continued: “There is still interest as well in Julian Alvarez.

"And with Atletico Madrid seemingly not willing to sell him to Barcelona, this is one where [Sporting director Andrea] Berta might just see an opportunity to steal a march on the Spanish giants.

“He's got a good relationship with Alvarez already, having negotiated his move from Manchester City to the Spanish capital. And that would be, for me, a game-changing signing for Arsenal.

"Someone who had a brilliant season last year. Didn’t really hit the heights of the World Cup. Wasn't even a first team starter for Argentina as they made it to the final, but I think he could be a really good addition for the Gunners.



“They've also been offered, we understand, Victor Osimhen during those conversations involving Gabriel Martinelli.

“He is on huge wages over in Turkey, but we do know Arsenal were willing to break the bank to pay Vinicius Jr in excess of £400,000. So maybe this one is not so fanciful as it sounds.

Sports.title: Why is Community Shield not at Wembley this weekend? Arsenal face Man City as season opener moved out of England
Sports.content:
Why is Community Shield not at Wembley this weekend? Arsenal face Man City as season opener moved out of England

The Community Shield is a staple of pre-season in England - but it will not be staged in the country for the first time in two decades.

Fans across the world will tune in as Premier League champions Arsenal take on FA Cup winners Manchester City this weekend.

3 Arsenal could be the team to beat again this season as they look to defend their crown in the Premier League Credit: Getty Images - Getty

The Gunners head into the match aiming to build on their title-winning campaign, following a long-awaited success last term.

Meanwhile, Enzo Maresca will manage his first game as Man City manager and kick off the post-Pep Guardiola era.

Why is the Community Shield not at Wembley Stadium this year?

A major change of venue will see the clash move away from Wembley Stadium to an iconic ground that last hosted the event in 2006.

This is due to scheduling issues with pre-planned summer concerts taking place at the traditional venue.

The Weeknd is booked at England's national football stadium, performing his 'After Hours Til Dawn Stadium Tour with Playboi Carti'.

The official statement released by the FA confirmed supporters will have to cross the border into Wales for the clash.

They stated: "The 2026 FA Community Shield will be played at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Sunday 16 August."

The event is historically held on the weekend before the Premier League commences, with this season on August 22.

This meant organisers had to target mid-August, which unfortunately clashed with the concert dates.

The Principality Stadium in Cardiff, a 74,500-capacity venue, offers a strictly neutral ground for both competing clubs, ensuring that fans of both teams face a journey.

3 Palace won the Community Shield at Wembley last year Credit: Getty

The Welsh national ground has hosted the Community Shield on six occasions between 2001 and 2006.

During that period, Arsenal played in four of the meetings, and won two.

Over the six years the fixture was relocated, only four teams competed across the border: Liverpool, Manchester United, Arsenal, and Chelsea.

In 2022, the fixture was also moved to the King Power Stadium due to Wembley Stadium hosting the Women's Euro 2022 final.

And in 2012, the game was also moved to Villa Park to host Man City and Chelsea as Wembley hosted the final of the 2012 Olympic football tournament.

The Manchester outfit were victorious on the day, winning 3-2.

3 Maresca's first competitive match in charge will be in Cardiff Credit: Getty

When is the Community Shield?

The 2026 FA Community Shield will take place this Sunday - August 16.

Kick-off for the match is scheduled for 3pm and will be held at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

talkSPORT will have coverage of the fixture, with commentary from Sam Matterface and former England captain Stuart Pearce.

To tune in to talkSPORT through the website, click HERE for the live stream or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app here.

Visit talkSPORT BET for all the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event.

Subscribe to our YouTube channel here for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

The FA Community Shield will be shown live in the UK on TNT Sports.

Recent Community Shield winners 2025: Crystal Palace

2024: Manchester City

2023: Arsenal

2022: Liverpool

2021: Leicester City

2020: Arsenal

2019: Manchester City

2018: Manchester City

2017: Arsenal

2016: Manchester United

2015: Arsenal

Who won the 2025 Community Shield?

Crystal Palace won last year's edition against Liverpool after securing their first-ever FA Cup.

The Eagles beat the Reds 3-2 on penalties at Wembley after playing out a 2-2 draw in normal time.

Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr scored for Palace in the draw, with Hugo Ekitike and Jeremie Frimpong netting for Liverpool.

Marc Guehi lifted the trophy as captain under Oliver Glasner, but he will be representing Man City on this year's occasion.

Similarly, Eberechi Eze also featured in a Palace shirt at Wembley last summer, but will be lining up for Arsenal instead.

Sports.title: Where to watch Community Shield: FA make change in 20-year first with Erling Haaland set to return for Man City
Sports.content:
Where to watch Community Shield: FA make change in 20-year first with Erling Haaland set to return for Man City

A rare Community Shield clash takes place this weekend as Arsenal face rivals Manchester City away from Wembley.

The Gunners feature after winning their first Premier League title in 22 years, coming up against Man City, who lifted the FA Cup.

3 Arsenal are playing in the Community Shield after winning the Premier League title Credit: Getty

Both Premier League giants are going to want to get their hands on the first domestic trophy available this campaign.

Their star-studded squads are more than used to playing at Wembley, but in a major change made by the FA, that is not where this year's game is going to be played.

Due to scheduling issues, the Community Shield will not be played at Wembley and instead at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

It is the first time in 20 years that this fixture has been played at the ground in Wales.

The game between Arsenal and Man City has been moved as music artist The Weeknd is booked in for concerts at Wembley.

So, Mikel Arteta and Enzo Maresca are going to have to travel with their squads over to Wales for the traditional season opener.

Where to watch Community Shield

The Community Shield will take place on Sunday, August 16.

Kick-off at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff is set for 3pm.

Fans can watch the game live on TV on TNT Sports, while the action will also be available to watch online via HBO Max.

Community Shield: Haaland returns

Erling Haaland has not featured at all in Man City's pre-season so far, having had an extended post-World Cup break.

But he's set to return to City training on Wednesday, along with record signing Elliot Anderson, Nico O'Reilly and Marc Guehi.

That only gives Haaland and the English trio five days back with the squad before the Community Shield takes place.

So, will they come straight back into the starting line-up? Or will Maresca take his time reintroducing them?

They are likely to play some part in the game, but it would be a boost for Arsenal if Haaland and co. weren't to start.

Sports.title: Community Shield LIVE commentary: Viktor Gyokeres confused by ‘friendly’ tag as Arsenal eye another trophy
Sports.content:
The Community Shield is often labelled a 'glorified friendly' - but Viktor Gyokeres doesn't appear to agree with that.

Gyokeres and Arsenal feature in the season opener this weekend as they take on Manchester City in Cardiff, live on talkSPORT.

2 Arsenal are confident heading into the new season after winning the title Credit: Getty

The reigning Premier League champions will be aiming to get their hands on some more silverware after success last season.

Meanwhile, FA Cup winners Man City are in the same boat, as new boss Enzo Maresca looks to get off to a perfect start.

And it seems there is going to be no lack of competitiveness when the two rivals do battle at the Principality Stadium.

During an interview last weekend, Gyokeres was asked how Arsenal would be approaching the Community Shield.

It was suggested that they could treat it as a 'friendly', but the Sweden international was bemused, asking: "What do you mean?"

After a follow-up explaining how the match can be seen as the final match of pre-season, a confused Gyokeres disagreed.

"I don't know what other people think, but of course we want to win that game for sure," the Gunners striker said. "There's no question about that."

Community Shield: talkSPORT coverage

Should all of the players involved share that same mentality, then Arsenal vs Manchester City is going to be a thriller.

The Community Shield will be played on Sunday, August 16 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, with kick-off at 3pm.

talkSPORT will have live commentary of the action from Sam Matterface and former England captain Stuart Pearce.

“I’m very happy, especially because the players since we started have been open-minded,” Maresca said on his side's progress. “They want to understand and want to learn why we do things.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola to Liverpool still alive as PSG consider cutting price in double boost
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola to Liverpool still alive as PSG consider cutting price in double boost

Liverpool have been handed a double boost in their pursuit of Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola.

The France international remains the Reds’ top summer transfer target but are yet to find a breakthrough in negotiations with the Champions League holders.



4 Bradley Barcola's potential move to Liverpool is still on the cards Credit: Getty

Barcola, who has two years remaining on his deal at the Parc des Princes, has informed PSG chiefs that he will not be renewing his contract at the club.

The 23-year-old made clear his desire to sign for Liverpool despite Arsenal also showing an interest.

He has also clarified that he will not push for a move away from the French capital this summer if a move away does not materialise.



PSG value Barcola at a whopping £145m - a price Liverpool are unwilling to pay.

Negotiations have been ongoing between the two clubs without significant progress, however talkSPORT’s chief football correspondent Alex Crook says there could now be a glimmer of hope for the Reds.



Crook's latest on the Barcola pursuit

“Liverpool fans are getting a little bit concerned about their lack of squad depth heading into the new season,” Crook said.

“It’s not been a brilliant pre-season campaign for Andoni Iraola.

“We know they’re keen on Bradley Barcola, we reported exclusively on talkSPORT.com some weeks ago now that he wanted to make the move to Anfield.



"But that £145m asking price set by PSG has been a real turn off for Liverpool.

“I’ve been told this morning that could come down a bit to £125m. That would equal the Premier League record fee that Liverpool paid for Alexander Isak.

4 Barcola was an unused substitute in Wednesday's UEFA Super Cup win over Aston Villa Credit: Getty

“I don’t think they have the appetite even to go that high for Barcola but PSG are bringing in reinforcements out wide.



“Ferran Torres is a done deal, he won’t be the only new arrival either.”

Liverpool could be further boosted by the imminent arrival of promising Ajax winger Mika Godts at the Parc des Princes.

The Belgian is set to fly to Paris on Wednesday to undergo a medical ahead of a £47.5m switch.

Godts primarily plays as a left winger with Kvicha Kvaratskhelia currently Luis Enrique’s first choice in that position ahead of Barcola.



Crook added: “If that does happen then surely they are going to have to lose someone and that’s maybe where Liverpool are maybe waiting in the wings for Bradley Barcola.

4 Mika Godts' impending move to PSG could open the door to Barcola's exit Credit: Getty

4 PSG youngster Ibrahim Mbaye is another possible option for the Reds Credit: Getty

“So just be a little bit patient Liverpool fans, this one is certainly not dead but they are not going to pay £145m or even £125m.”



Barcola appears more likely to make the switch to Anfield than PSG academy graduate Ibrahim Mbaye.

The Senegalese starlet fell out of favour with Luis Enrique at the end of last season with PSG reportedly open to the player’s exit in the event of a significant offer.

Liverpool have shown an interest in Mbaye as they look to fill the gap left by Mohamed Salah’s departure.

There are no guarantees that the 18-year-old will leave PSG this summer and much will depend on Liverpool’s outlay on a possible Barcola deal.

Sports.title: Serie A Como interested in signing Chelsea forward Liam Delap - as Arsenal hold talks over signing Victor Osimhen amid interest in Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Wigan sign City star

Manchester City defender Finley Burns has signed a permanent deal with League One Wigan Athletic.

The 23-year-old has been with City since he was 13-years-old, becoming a commanding presence in their elite development squad.

The England youth international was part of City's 2020-21 Premier League 2 winning side, making 16 league appearances at centre-back and was handed his senior debut by Pep Guardiola in City’s 6-1 Carabao Cup triumph over Wycombe Wanderers in September 2021 before joining Swansea City on a season's loan.

Man City defender Finley Burns has signed a permanent deal with League One Wigan Athletic

Como keen on Delap

Como have registered interest in Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

The Italian side wish to take him on loan, while Chelsea value the 23-year-old at around £55m.

Arsenal's Osimhen interest

Arsenal have discussed signing Victor Osimhen during talks with Galatasaray over the potential sales of Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri.

Galatasaray made a £38.5million verbal offer for Martinelli, but the 25-year-old Brazilian is reluctant to leave London.

Nwaneri, 19, meanwhile, is assessing his options and, as it stands, talks for Nigeria striker Osimhen have not progressed.

Arsenal also hold an interest in Jarell Quansah and have made contact with the England defender's representatives.

Bayer Leverkusen do not wish to sell the 23-year-old but Arsenal want to be aware of the parameters and know he would be open to joining them.

Liverpool have the option to match any offer for Quansah as part of the deal that led to him joining the Bundesliga club last year, but it is understood they have no intention of actioning their clause.

They are continuing talks for Ezri Konsa but Aston Villa's valuation has been prohibitive for the deal they want.

Victor Osimhen's name was discussed by Arsenal transfer chiefs this summer

Martinelli has had tentative interest from Paris Saint-Germain in recent weeks, but the French side have now turned their attention to Ajax’s Mika Godts, 21.

England Under-21 international Nwaneri was frustrated with a lack of game time last season, but has interest from AC Milan, Fulham, RB Leipzig and Borussia Dortmund, among others.

Arsenal are also in talks with West Ham over the £3m sale of winger Reiss Nelson, and Napoli want striker Gabriel Jesus.

There is interest from Hamburg for Fabio Vieira, and fellow midfielder Martin Zubimendi is on the radar of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid.

Barca prepare next Rodri offer

Barcelona are drafting a new proposal for Manchester City midfielder Rodri after their second offer was rejected. City are holding for closer £68m for the Spain captain.

Rodri was spotted by fans travelling back to Liverpool airport on a Ryanair flight from Madrid on Thursday evening.

City have rejected two bids from Barcelona for the midfielder, the second of which was around £55m.

Rodri is waiting on Barcelona and Man City to agree a fee for his move back to Spain

Scanlon heading to south Wales

Liverpool left back Calum Scanlon is expected to finalise his loan move to Cardiff today.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff and they have been working hard to bring him back.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and attracted a number of enquiries. League One Sheffield Wednesday, notably, made concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Liverpool midfielder James McConnell is a loan target for Championship side Preston. A number of other Championship teams have enquired for the 21-year-old plus League One Leicester.

Wrexham set sights on Souttar

Wrexham are hoping to close a deal for Leicester defender Harry Souttar this weekend.

The Welsh side offered around £7.5million for the Australia international earlier this week and hope to have the edge over rivals Sheffield United who have also been bidding for the 27-year-old centre back.

Hammers smash transfer record for Engels

West Ham have agreed a Championship record transfer fee worth £22million for Celtic midfielder Arne Engels.

The Belgium international is due to undergo a medical in London today with the Hammers who have a long-held interest in the 22-year-old and had previously had two bids rejected by Celtic last month.

The previous record transfer fee is £17.5m paid by Ipswich Town to Nordsjaelland for Sindre Walle Egeli.

Marseille move for Perri

Marseille are continuing talks for Leeds goalkeeper Lucas Perri.

The Brazilian, who joined Leeds from Lyon, had been lined up for a loan to Torino and was even scheduled for medical but Marseille have been pushing this week to convince him of their project after selling Geronimo Rulli to Manchester City.

Rulli was bought as cover after James Trafford was sold to Leeds, who are closing on an £8.2m deal for Borussia Monchengladbach centre back Nico Elvedi. The Switzerland international, 29, can also play at right back.

Meanwhile, Marseille have also enquired about Arsenal forward Reiss Nelson.

The 26-year-old has been discussing a £3m move to West Ham but is unsure about dropping to the Championship.

Tigers' Calvin heading out on loan

Hull's rising young prospect Calvin Okike is being eyed for a loan move.

The 18-year-old left back opted to sign professional forms with the Tigers early this summer, a two-year deal with the option of a third, despite being closely monitored by several top Premier League clubs and has done well in pre-season working with the first team.

He largely featured for the U21s last season but was an unused substitute in a 2-0 win over Norwich City in the Championship.

Okike had a loan spell at National League club Hartlepool United this year, scoring within a minute of his senior debut and has featured in Hull's recent friendly victories over Turkish sides Konyaspor and Caykur Rizespor.

He won the academy player of the year award last season and is drawing attention from League One Barnsley, Plymouth Argyle, Bristol Rovers, Port Vale and Oldham Athletic.

Everton keen on Wheatley

Manchester United and Everton are continuing discussions over the transfer of Ethan Wheatley.

The 20-year-old striker is viewed as one for the future by Everton but will be able to have an impact in the first team.

The England Under-20 international is 6ft 3in and regularly clocks 36km/h in sprints. He has been on loan at Northampton Town and Bradford City in recent seasons and was a prolific scorer through youth levels at United.

United winger Ethan Williams has joined Peterborough for an undisclosed fee. United’s deal also includes add-ons, a 50 per cent sell-on clause, a buy-back option and matching rights.

Spence ready for Italian job

Tottenham full back Djed Spence arrived in Milan last night ahead of his £26m move to Inter.

The 26-year-old has started his medical tests at the CONI Sports Medicine Institute this morning.

.@Inter, Spence è arrivato al CONI per l’idoneità sportiva pic.twitter.com/vYZESpNdfX — Gianluca Di Marzio (@DiMarzio) August 14, 2026

Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr is emerging as a target for Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League. The 23-year-old will be allowed to leave and has been the subject of interest from Brentford and Aston Villa as well as other European sides.

Juventus have revived talks for Spurs keeper Guglielmo Vicario while defender Cristian Romero will have his medical with Atletico Madrid tomorrow.

Spurs remain in talks for Manchester City winger Savinho and Cody Gakpo of Liverpool. City’s Omar Marmoush is also on their list.

Badiashile set for Napoli switch

Napoli have agreed a deal with Chelsea to sign defender Benoit Badiashile on an initial loan for £2.5m that could rise to £3.4m with an option to buy permanently for around £23m.

Celtic are closing in on a loan for Chelsea full back Landon Emenalo.

Where there's a Will, there's a way

Will Smallbone has emerged as a target for West Brom. The 26-year-old midfielder is a free agent after leaving Southampton.

The Republic of Ireland international has a number of options but Albion have emerged as they are losing Alex Mowatt to Derby.

Benda heading to Forest

Nottingham Forest are signing Fulham goalkeeper Steven Benda on a free transfer. He is due for a medical today.

Tiger Tim

Hull have formalised their interest in Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam with an offer understood to be in excess of £15million. The 23-year-old has a year left on contract.

Leeds forward Joe Gelhardt has completed his medical at Hull ahead of his £4.5million move.

So Burnley bound

Brazilian side Palmeiras have signed Fabio So from Burnley.

Zaha returns home

Free agent Wilfried Zaha is training alone at former club Crystal Palace while he searches for a new club.

Howell heads to Leicester

Brighton midfielder Harry Howell has joined Leicester on a season's loan.
