World.title: Osun election: IPAC urges peaceful poll, tasks security on credible election
World.content:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

The Inter-Party Advisory Council, IPAC, Osun State chapter urged political stakeholders and electorates to ensure the August 15 governorship election is conducted peacefully and without rancour.

The Chairman of IPAC in the state, Dr Tosin Odeyemi of the Democratic Leadership Alliance, made the call in a statement issued in Osogbo on Friday.

Odeyemi stated that Saturday’s election provides Osun people another opportunity to choose leaders that will drive development in the state, urging the electorate to vote their conscience.

The DLA chairman urged all registered voters to come out en masse to exercise their franchise, noting that abstaining from voting only leaves room for undemocratic elements to decide the state’s future.

He said, “Going to vote is your civic responsibility. Do not sell your vote. Do not allow anyone to intimidate you. Your PVC is your power to determine who governs you for the next four years.”

The IPAC chairman also called on security agencies deployed for the election to be professional, neutral and up and doing in the discharge of their duties.

“The duty is to protect voters, electoral officials, materials and result collation centres across the 30 local government areas of the state. You must ensure you do your job diligently without compromise.

“Any act of ballot snatching, thuggery or violence must be dealt with decisively in line with the law,” Odeyemi stated.

He further appealed to parents and guardians to warn their wards against being used as political thugs or for any act capable of disrupting the peace of the state.

World.title: Political class biggest threat to Nigeria’s security – ASUU
World.content:
Piwuna

Union authorises strike in PLASU, 12 other universities over 2025 agreement

By Golok Nanmwa

The Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, has described the political class as the biggest threat to Nigeria’s security, warning that rising political killings, thuggery and pre-election violence could plunge the country into a major crisis ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The union also authorised affected branches in Plateau State University, Bokkos, PLASU, and other federal and state-owned universities to commence processes leading to industrial action over the non-implementation of the December 2025 agreement reached with the Federal Government.

ASUU’s National Executive Council, NEC, took the decisions at its meeting held at the University of Abuja on August 8 and 9, 2026, where it reviewed developments in the education sector, economy, politics and security.

In a statement signed by its National President, Prof. Christopher Piwuna, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Friday, the union said recent political developments had created palpable fears among Nigerians as the country approaches the 2027 elections.

According to ASUU, the political atmosphere is increasingly being “toxified by thuggery, brigandage and political killings fueled by entrenched politics of bitterness and winner-takes-all.”

The union warned that the situation had compounded the country’s already serious insecurity challenges, including threats to educational and religious institutions.

ASUU said, “As things stand now, the political class are the most significant and dangerous threat to Nigeria’s security. They are the ‘tribe’ that threatens us all.”

It further warned that if the current signals persisted, “the simmering tension may soon erupt like a volcano in the face of everybody.”

The union also accused the ruling class of worsening the country’s problems through corruption, procurement violations, questionable contract awards and failure to prioritise critical infrastructure.

It specifically challenged claims by the Rural Electrification Agency that solar farms had been installed and connected to 15 Nigerian universities.

ASUU said information received from its branches showed that some of the installations were either not functioning or had suffered repeated breakdowns.

The union urged governments to embrace transparency and accountability, arguing that citizens could not trust authorities whose promises were repeatedly raised and dashed.

On the university system, ASUU expressed strong dissatisfaction with the continued non-payment of the outstanding three-and-a-half months’ salaries owed lecturers following the 2022 nationwide strike.

It recalled that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had initially paid four of the seven-and-a-half months withheld by the previous administration, but said the outstanding balance had remained unpaid.

The union said lecturers had made significant sacrifices to recover lost academic time after the strike and that payment of the remaining balance would help strengthen industrial harmony in the nation’s universities.

ASUU therefore resolved to deploy all legitimate means available to compel government to pay the outstanding salaries.

The union also demanded immediate payment of the 25/35 per cent wage award and promotion arrears owed its members, warning that the continued delay was increasing frustration among lecturers.

On the December 2025 FGN-ASUU agreement, the union described its implementation as haphazard and warned that the situation could lead to renewed unrest on university campuses.

According to ASUU, federal universities, including universities of agriculture, were struggling to implement the financial components of the agreement because of inadequate government funding.

At the state level, it said only about 10 per cent or fewer governors had openly endorsed the new salary package for academics, while several others were allegedly shifting responsibility to governing councils without providing the required financial backing.

Consequently, NEC resolved to grant affected branches permission to embark on varying degrees of industrial action after satisfying the necessary requirements.

Among the institutions listed by the union are Nasarawa State University, Keffi; Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida University, Lapai; University of Medical Sciences, Ondo; Gombe State University; Plateau State University, Bokkos; Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba; Ambrose Alli University, Ekpoma; Olusegun Agagu University of Science and Technology, Okitipupa; Abia State University, Uturu; University of Education and Entrepreneurship, Akamkpa; Emmanuel Alayande University of Education, Oyo; Kaduna State University; and Aliko Dangote University of Science and Technology, Wudil.

Recent reports on the NEC resolution indicate that affected branches have been directed to commence preparations for industrial action, with the union’s move linked to the failure of governments to implement the 2025 agreement.

ASUU further lamented the continued underfunding of education, saying the declining real value of budgetary allocations had weakened infrastructure, crippled research and undermined teaching and learning.

The union said Nigeria’s rapidly growing population was not matched by corresponding investment in critical sectors, particularly education and healthcare.

It also criticised the rising cost of healthcare, energy and agricultural production, saying the situation had made basic necessities increasingly unaffordable for Nigerians.

ASUU called on the Federal and subnational governments to prioritise agricultural and industrial production, social protection and people-oriented development.

It urged government to suspend unnecessary borrowing, recover stolen public resources, block leakages and strengthen accountability.

The union said Nigeria was at a critical juncture and that the people must be placed at the centre of government policies as the country moves towards the 2027 elections.

It also called for a comprehensive review of the nation’s education system to reflect Nigeria’s socio-economic, cultural, technological and developmental realities.

ASUU said greater attention must be given to research, technical education, agriculture, innovation and skills development.

It urged the Federal and state governments to urgently resolve all outstanding welfare issues affecting academic staff and fully implement matters arising from the December 2025 FGN-ASUU agreement in order to prevent further disruption of academic activities.

The union warned that failure to address the issues could further deepen industrial unrest in Nigerian universities.

World.title: Arteta expects Maresca to do ‘unbelievable job’ at Man City
World.content:
Arsenal’s Spanish manager Mikel Arteta attends a press conference at the Emirates Stadium in London on May 4, 2026, on the eve of their UEFA Champions League league semifinal, second-leg football match against Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP)

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has backed Enzo Maresca to do an “unbelievable job” after replacing Pep Guardiola as Manchester City manager.

Premier League champions Arsenal and FA Cup holders City meet in the Community Shield in Cardiff on Sunday in Maresca’s first showpiece occasion since Guardiola quit at the end of last season.

Arteta, once Guardiola’s assistant at City, paid tribute to his old boss during a pre-match press conference on Friday but expects Arsenal’s title rivals to remain a force under former Chelsea manager Maresca.

“First of all for the Premier League, I think for the country, I think the way he has opened a different way of understanding the game. Here, I think he has escalated the Premier League to a different level,” Arteta said of Guardiola, who won 20 major trophies during his 10-year spell in charge of City.

“I was very lucky to be part of that for four years and understand and witness how it’s done daily. I think it’s remarkable and unique.

“I would say that he’s the best coach in the history of football. For many reasons, he’s done it in different countries, in different ways. So, I think he will be missed in the Premier League.”

City won the FA Cup and League Cup in Guardiola’s final season but finished as Premier League runners-up behind Arsenal.

Arteta, who ended Arsenal’s 22-year wait for a Premier League title, added: “It’s been a pleasure and now it’s Enzo. I know him well and he will provide something different to the club.

“What I know is that Enzo has the personality, the character, and especially the knowledge to have an unbelievable job there.

“That’s why he’s been selected, because they could probably pick anybody and they’ve gone for Enzo for the right reasons.

“He has demonstrated that at every level. What he’s done in the Champions League and what he’s done, when he’s been at Chelsea and now here, so I have no doubt that he will do a great job.”

Arteta said England duo Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka could be involved in the Community Shield, with new signings Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis also likely to feature.

“We are really excited to start the season, to start with the first trophy,” said Arteta. “All the internationals are back and we can’t wait to start competing.

“The best version has to be on Sunday and that’s the intention, that we have the best performance and the best way to start the season by lifting the first trophy.”

Arteta gave little away on reports the Gunners are looking to sign Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah after failing to convince Aston Villa to sell Ezri Konsa.

“I’m not going to talk about any individuals (elsewhere),” he said. “Obviously what I can tell you is the ambition of the club.

“We want to improve the squad, we want to evolve the squad in order to achieve that.”

AFP

World.title: Hospital collapses after landslide in Calabar
World.content:
A hospital building in Calabar, the Cross River State capital, has collapsed following a landslide triggered by heavy rainfall.

The affected structure, identified as UNICEM Hospital, reportedly gave way on Thursday, August 13, after hours of torrential rain destabilised the hillside on which it was built.

Videos circulating on social media showed parts of the hospital collapsing as residents watched from a safe distance. A Calabar-based pharmacist, Mekzy, who shared one of the videos on X, attributed the incident to a landslide caused by the heavy downpour.

There was no official confirmation of casualties as of Friday. Although eyewitness accounts indicated that the collapse caused panic in the area, emergency authorities had yet to confirm whether anyone was trapped or injured.

Footage from the scene showed a large mass of earth sliding into the hospital complex before sections of the building collapsed, leaving behind concrete debris and exposed reinforcement rods.

The incident has renewed concerns about Calabar’s vulnerability to landslides, flooding and erosion during the rainy season. The report also noted concerns over development on unstable slopes, inadequate drainage and weak enforcement of building regulations.

The collapse is expected to trigger renewed calls for stricter building controls and proper geotechnical assessments before construction in areas prone to erosion and landslides.

As of the time of filing, neither the Cross River State Government nor emergency management agencies had issued a detailed statement on the incident.

World.title: Ex IGP Adamu empowers Nasarawa farmers, urges politicians to support food production
World.content:
Former Inspector-General of Police and Social Democratic Party governorship candidate in Nasarawa State, Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, has called on politicians and other individuals with the means to support farmers as part of efforts to tackle food insecurity and reduce poverty in the state.



Adamu made the call on Wednesday while launching an agricultural empowerment programme for farmers in Nasarawa’s western zone, covering Keffi, Karu, Kokona, Nasarawa and Toto local government areas.

The programme, held at the premises of the Esu Karu Palace in Karu, featured the distribution of farm equipment and inputs to hundreds of beneficiaries.

Adamu said the initiative was designed to increase agricultural production, strengthen food security and improve the livelihoods of farmers across the state.

“We are not just here to support and empower our farmers but to introduce them to modern farming methods and implements that will aid in the production of more food for our people. We are empowering our farmers for increased food production and sustainable livelihoods,” he said.



The SDP candidate noted that Nasarawa was predominantly agrarian but said farmers had continued to face challenges, including inadequate modern equipment and low-yielding crops, which had limited their ability to expand production.

He said his administration, if elected, would prioritise agriculture as part of its strategy to address hunger and poverty.

“In line with my manifesto we hold the view and very strongly too that working together with our farmers we can end hunger and reduce poverty in Nasarawa State,” Adamu said.

He urged politicians across the state to complement government efforts by investing in farmers, stressing that increased food production would eventually translate into lower prices and greater availability of food.

“So whether you are a politician or not, if you have the means, please come out and also assist the farmers. Come out, out of the little that you have, assist the farmers. Because when you assist them, we are going to get more food. If you have more food in the market, the food will be cheap and everybody will get it,” he said.

The former police chief said the empowerment scheme was not intended to compete with government programmes but to complement them.

“We know the government is trying its best to provide for the people of Nasarawa, but we know they will never be able to do it for everybody. So let them not think that we are competing with them, no. We are only contributing our own quota,” he said.

Items distributed included 100 tricycles, 200 soil-tilling machines, 2,500 herbicides, 1,200 litres of organic fertiliser, 1,500 bags of NPK and urea, 500 knapsack sprayers and other farm implements.

Adamu said the programme would be extended to other parts of Nasarawa in the coming weeks.

World.title: Trump asks US Supreme Court to approve White House ballroom project
World.content:
The Trump administration asked the US Supreme Court on Friday to allow it to complete construction of a ballroom and secure underground bunker at the White House, saying the project was essential for national security.

Solicitor General John Sauer made the request in an emergency appeal to the conservative-dominated top court, which includes three justices nominated by President Donald Trump.

Trump ordered the demolition of the historic East Wing of the White House last year to make way for a massive ballroom but the project has been tied up in the lower courts.

An appeals court last week upheld a district court order halting work on the ballroom but put its ruling on hold to allow for the administration to appeal to the Supreme Court.

The US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit agreed with the lower court that such a sweeping White House overhaul required the explicit consent of Congress.

Trump lashed out after the 2-1 ruling, calling it “horrendous, politically motivated, and unlawful,” and said he would appeal to the Supreme Court.

The president initially touted the construction of the ballroom as being necessary to host galas and state dinners, but has since repeatedly pointed to the addition of an underground military bunker and other security features.

The solicitor general, in the appeal to the Supreme Court, also emphasized the security aspects of the project.

“This case involves an extraordinary and unlawful injunction that will halt the ongoing construction of the integrated military complex, including a totally secure ballroom space, at the East Wing of the White House, which is vitally required by national security,” Sauer said.

“The President of the United States of America is not a tenant, but rather the sole, elected head of the Executive Branch, and Congress has authorized him to renovate, secure, and protect the White House and its grounds, as other Presidents have been allowed to do, without exception,” he added.

Work on the project began last year with the sudden demolition of the East Wing, which used to house the offices of the first lady.

Trump has insisted that the ballroom will be privately financed, but media reports in June showed that significant taxpayer funds were going to the project, which could cost as much as $600 million.

The ballroom is just one of Trump’s pet projects to leave his mark on Washington by the time his second term ends in January 2029, along with a renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other parks, and construction of a gigantic arch.

Several of the projects have similarly faced legal challenges, but the ballroom project is the first to reach the Supreme Court.

AFP

World.title: 10 African countries with the highest total rail coverage in 2026
World.content:
File image

Railway networks remain an important part of Africa’s transport infrastructure, connecting major cities, industrial centres, ports and agricultural regions while supporting trade and economic activity.

According to 2026 data from Global Firepower, South Africa has by far the largest total rail coverage on the continent, with more than 30,000 kilometres of railway lines.

Sudan ranks second with 7,251km, followed by Egypt with 5,085km. Mozambique and Tanzania complete the top five, with 4,787km and 4,097km respectively.

Algeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Nigeria and Zimbabwe also feature among the African countries with the largest railway networks.

Here are the top 10 African countries with the highest total rail coverage in 2026:

South Africa – 30,400km Sudan – 7,251km Egypt – 5,085km Mozambique – 4,787km Tanzania – 4,097km Algeria – 4,020km Democratic Republic of the Congo – 4,007km Kenya – 3,819km Nigeria – 3,798km Zimbabwe – 3,427km

South Africa ranks eighth globally, while Sudan is the second-highest-ranked African country at 31st worldwide.

Nigeria, with 3,798km of total rail coverage, ranks ninth in Africa and 51st globally.

Vanguard News

World.title: NFF sets up committee to investigate Super Falcons’ World Cup failure
World.content:
Super Falcons

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has set up a fact-finding committee to investigate the country’s recent struggles in international football, with particular attention on the Super Falcons’ failure to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

The decision follows Nigeria’s disappointing campaign at the ongoing Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco, where the Super Falcons were eliminated in the quarter-finals before suffering a 2-1 defeat to South Africa in the playoff for a place in the Inter-Confederation Playoffs.

The defeat means Nigeria will miss the 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil, bringing an end to the Super Falcons’ record of appearing at every edition of the tournament since its inaugural staging in 1991.

The NFF said the committee would examine the setbacks suffered by the national teams and make recommendations aimed at preventing a repeat of such failures.

Ambassador Fanny Amun, MON, will chair the committee, while former Nigeria internationals Ladan Bosso, Desire Oparanozie and Mutiu Adepoju, alongside Dr Alex Mana, will serve as members.

Mr Nasiru Jibril has been appointed secretary of the committee.

The NFF said the committee’s findings and recommendations will help guide measures to improve Nigeria’s performance in future international competitions.

Vanguard News

World.title: 2027: FG Calls on Youths to Participate in Electoral Process
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Federal Government has called on youths to participate actively in the Nigerian electoral process with a view to driving the economic growth and development agenda they envision for the country.

The government said many democracies, including Nigeria, are confronted with the challenges of declining trust, voter apathy, misinformation, vote buying, electoral violence and the growing perception among young people that their votes do not make a meaningful difference.

Speaking at the Election Roundtable on the 2027 general election, jointly organised by the Humanitarian Foundation for Social Justice and The Create Studio Nigeria in Abuja, the Director of Civic, Values and Democracy Education at the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Dr Olukemi Afolayan, said reclaiming votes must begin with reclaiming citizens’ confidence in the democratic process.

She said: “Nigeria is a youthful nation. Our young people are not merely the leaders of tomorrow; they are active stakeholders in the Nigeria of today. Their voices, choices and participation will significantly determine the quality of our democracy and the future of our country.

“Enfranchising a new generation of voters therefore requires more than encouraging young people to register and vote. It requires equipping them with the knowledge, confidence and civic values to participate meaningfully and responsibly.

“At the National Orientation Agency, we believe that civic education and values reorientation are essential pillars of democratic development. Citizens must understand not only how to vote, but why their vote matters; not only their rights, but also their responsibilities.”

She said the government must empower voters to reject vote buying and selling, resist manipulation and misinformation, shun electoral violence and demand issue-based campaigns from political actors.

“We must also create a democratic environment where every eligible citizen, especially young people, women and persons with disabilities, feels that the political process belongs to them,” she said.

The keynote speaker, Prof. Ajibade Abiodun Michael, urged the government at all levels to invest in two things: “Reclaiming our vote from the forces of apathy and obstruction, and enfranchising a new generation that is ready to lead.”

He noted that the right to vote is the oxygen of democracy, adding: “Yet, for too long, we have been holding our breath. Voter suppression is not a relic of the past; it is a sophisticated, evolving art. From the purging of voter rolls to the closure of polling places in minority neighbourhoods, from strict voter ID laws that solve a problem that does not exist to gerrymandering that makes your vote feel like a drop in a rigged ocean, the message is clear: stay home. Your voice does not matter.”

He urged the electoral umpire to invest more in technology, arguing that technology is not the enemy of elections but an enabler.

In his goodwill message, the Executive Director of the Justice, Development and Peace Caritas Initiative (JDPCI), Catholic Archdiocese of Abuja, Rev. Fr Sebastian Sanni, said the future of Nigeria’s democracy could not be discussed without placing young people at the centre of the conversation.

Represented by the Programmes Director, JDPC Abuja, Mr Timothy Ejeh, the Executive Director said: “Nigerian youths have the numbers. They have the energy. They have the creativity. They have the capacity. What remains is the courage to use their collective power responsibly.”

Earlier, in his welcome address, the Executive Director of the Humanitarian Foundation for Social Justice, Adekunle Adebanjo, said the roundtable was conceived as a platform for constructive engagement among critical stakeholders.

“We have gathered to examine the forthcoming 2027 general election by reflecting on the gains already recorded in our democratic journey, identifying the challenges confronting our electoral process, and collectively proffering practical solutions that can strengthen our democracy,” Adebanjo said.

World.title: At Washington Talks, Nigeria Reinforces Defence, Security Partnership with US
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Federal Government has reinforced its defence and security partnership with the United States Government with a view to deepening military-to-military relations and strengthening counter-terrorism cooperation between Nigeria and the United States.

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), stated this during a high-level bilateral engagement with the United States Government in Washington, D.C.

During a strategic meeting at the Pentagon, the Defence Minister was joined by a high-powered Nigerian delegation that included the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele; the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede; the Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lt Gen Parker Udiandeye; and other senior officers from the Armed Forces of Nigeria.

According to a statement by the Special Assistant on Media to the Minister of Defence, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the Nigerian delegation held robust discussions with senior cabinet officials of the U.S. Department of War, led by the Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for International Security Affairs, Julia Sokol.

The engagement, she said, served as a direct continuation of the United States-Nigeria Joint Working Group Defence Bilateral Talks, focusing on shared security architecture, intelligence collaboration and operational synergies.

Mrs Katung-Babatunde said the diplomatic mission, led by the National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, was made up of senior government officials who were in the United States of America for the second meeting of the US-Nigeria Joint Working Group, held from 12 to 13 August 2026.

Co-chaired by Mallam Nuhu Ribadu and Allison Hooker, the U.S. Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs, the meeting reviewed actionable progress and strategic frameworks following Nigeria’s designation as a Country of Particular Concern (CPC).

“Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to sustained dialogue, mutual respect and strategic alliance in combating global and regional threats,” the statement said.

World.title: Adegoke Remains Oyo ADC Guber Candidate, Says Media Team
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The Media Team of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Oyo State, Adegboyega Taofeek Adegoke, on Friday, described the claim to the party’s governorship ticket by one of the gubernatorial aspirants, Mr. Gbemileke Alagbe, as “wishful thinking”.

This is just as it questioned how Alagbe could claim to be the ADC governorship candidate after instituting a suit against the party and its National Working Committee (NWC).

Alagbe had on Thursday during a press conference stated that he is the ADC candidate in the 2027 general election, and unveiled Mr. Niyi Aborisade as his running mate and deputy governorship candidate.

But the media team cited Suit No. FHC/IB/CS/67/2026, filed by him at the Federal High Court in Ibadan on June 28, 2026, stating that the case had been adjourned until September 15, 2026.

“How can someone that has already taken the ADC, the ADC NWC and others to court be claiming he is the governorship candidate submitted by the same party, ADC, to INEC? Is that not a contradiction?” the team asked.

It also questioned the basis of Alagbe’s decision to sue the party and subsequently claim that the same party had submitted his name to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

It maintained that Adegoke emerged as the ADC governorship candidate at the party’s primary election with 16,051 votes.

According to the team, the primary election results, which were publicly reported by multiple media organisations, showed Bisi Ilaka with 11,415 votes, Alagbe with 241 votes, Azeez Adeduntan with 155 votes and Aborisade with 67 votes.

It therefore urged the media, members of the public and ADC members in the state to disregard what it described as false claims concerning the party’s governorship ticket.

It said: “The identity of a political party’s candidate is not determined by who makes the loudest declaration or who receives the most publicity. It is determined by the applicable electoral process, authentic records and the law.

“For the avoidance of doubt, Olooye Adegboyega Taofeek Adegoke remains our recognised gubernatorial candidate, and we remain firmly committed to defending his mandate through every lawful and legitimate avenue available to us.

“We have no objection to any individual exercising his or her lawful rights, but we will strongly resist any attempt to substitute propaganda, wishful thinking, or unverifiable claims for established facts.”

World.title: Tinubu To INEC, Security Agencies: Ensure Peaceful, Transparent Poll In Osun
World.content:
* Says outcome of Osun election must reflect will of the citizenry

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the security agencies to ensure a peaceful and transparent election in Osun State.

The people of Osun State will go to the polls on Saturday, August 15, 2026, to elect their governor in an election where 15 candidates are contesting.

Among them are the incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate, Hon. Najeem Salaam.

The president, in a release issued on Friday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, also charged the electorate in Osun State to come out to discharge their civic responsibility and eschew any act that could disrupt the peaceful conduct of the election, while assuring the people of their safety before and after the polls.

“As the people of Osun State head to the polling units to elect who will govern them in the next four years, I call on the Independent National Electoral Commission to ensure orderly conduct of the election. The election must be transparent, free and fair. I urge INEC to ensure the integrity of the process,” Tinubu said.

“INEC must use this last off-cycle election as a test case to demonstrate to Nigerians their full preparedness for the 2027 polls,” he added.

“I have charged the Inspector-General of Police and other heads of security outfits taking part in the election to provide maximum security at polling units. No room should be allowed for troublemakers to disrupt the process.

“Electoral officials and voters must be protected so they can perform their civic duties without fear or intimidation.

“Voters should feel confident to go out in their numbers to vote for the candidate of their choice as all measures necessary to ensure a peaceful, free and fair election have been put in place.

“Our elections must be credible, and the outcome of the Osun governorship election must reflect the will of the people,” the president declared.

World.title: RATTAWU Extols Adeola Ajayi’s Integrity, Competence, Applauds Tinubu for Appointing Him as DSS DG
World.content:
The Radio, Television, Theatre and Arts Workers Union (RATTAWU) has applauded President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for appointing Mr Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi as the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), describing him as a man of valour, integrity, competence and proven capacity.

The commendation was made by the RATTAWU President, Comrade Prince Emeka Kalu, during the union’s Media/Security critical engagement and strategic partnership for national development.

During the engagement, the DSS Director-General was conferred with the Golden Era Pillar of Critical and Strategic Intelligence for National Development Award.

The initiative is designed to recognise individuals and institutions that have made outstanding contributions to national development, security, democracy, culture and the growth of Nigeria.

Speaking during the visit, Kalu commended President Tinubu for appointing Ajayi to lead the nation’s foremost domestic intelligence organisation.

He described the DSS Director-General as a silent achiever, a competent and detribalised Nigerian and a man whose commitment to national service transcends ethnic, religious and political considerations.

According to the RATTAWU President, the appointment demonstrates the importance of placing capable Nigerians with integrity and professional competence in strategic positions of national responsibility.

He further noted that the role of the DSS in protecting Nigeria’s National interests, gathering critical intelligence and supporting National security cannot be overemphasised, particularly at a time when the Country is confronted with complex security and emerging technological challenges.

Kalu said RATTAWU, as a Union representing workers across the radio, television, theatre and arts sectors, has a responsibility to contribute to National development by using its platforms to promote responsible communication, peace, unity and democratic values.

He stated that RATTAWU Nigeria would continue to provide platforms for the sensitisation of citizens, especially as the nation prepares for the forthcoming general election.

He stressed that the media and creative sectors have an important role to play in combating misinformation, promoting tolerance and encouraging citizens to participate responsibly in the democratic process.

Kalu also emphasised the need for stronger collaboration between security agencies, the media, creative professionals and organised labour in building a peaceful and cohesive Nigeria.

Responding, the DSS Director-General expressed appreciation to the leadership of RATTAWU for the exceptional honour bestowed on him.

He described the recognition as a significant gesture that would further encourage him and the Service to remain committed to their responsibilities to the nation.

Ajayi encouraged RATTAWU to remain steadfast in upholding values that promote national cohesion, tolerance, peace and unity, noting that such values are essential to the continued stability and development of Nigeria.

He assured the Union of his willingness to remain available for constructive engagement, particularly in areas that could create meaningful networks, partnerships and collaboration between the DSS and RATTAWU.

The Director-General expressed optimism that such engagements would strengthen institutional cooperation and contribute to greater national cohesion.

World.title: Security Chiefs, Katsina Govt Intensify War against Banditry, Terrorism
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

Security chiefs, Katsina State Government and other stakeholders in the state have called for stronger synergy, intelligence sharing, and coordinated operations among security agencies to defeat terrorism, banditry and other criminal activities threatening the Northwest region of the country.

The call was made at the North-west Conference of State Directors of Security held in Katsina yesterday with the theme: ‘Unite Against Terror.’

Speaking at the conference, the Katsina State Director of the Department of State Services (DSS), Alhassan Iliyasu, said there’s collaboration among security agencies, communities and other stakeholders to effectively tackle terrorism, banditry and other criminal activities in the region.

He said the fight against terrorism and banditry could not be won by security agencies alone, stressing that every member of society had a role to play in providing useful information and supporting security operations to tackle the region’s evolving security challenges.

He added that the conference provided an opportunity for heads of intelligence-led organisations and security agencies across the region to review emerging threats, share experiences and develop renewed strategies for curbing banditry and related criminal activities.

Iliyasu said: “The purpose of this conference is for us to come together, review the nitty-gritty of the security challenges, come up with renewed strategies and scale up our countermeasures.”

He noted that the collaboration among security agencies, community-based security structures, vigilante groups and other stakeholders would significantly improve responses to security threats across the northwest region of the country.

He commended the Director-General of the DSS, Mr. Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi, for providing renewed direction for the Service and creating opportunities to strengthen its intelligence and tactical capabilities.

On his part, the Commander, 17 Brigade, Nigerian Army, Katsina, Brigadier-General Ishaya Ibrahim, explained that the synergy among security agencies was no longer an advantage but an imperative in confronting the evolving and borderless nature of terrorism.

He disclosed that military firepower and territorial operations alone could not defeat terrorists, adding that actionable intelligence remained critical to the success of military operations.

He said terrorists exploit gaps in information, coordination and trust, hence the need for the nation’s security agencies to bridge such gaps through real-time intelligence sharing, joint operational planning and mutual support.

In his opening remarks, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda said Katsina State had recorded significant improvements in its security challenges through a combination of both kinetic and non-kinetic measures.

Represented by his Deputy, Faruk Lawal, the governor attributed the security improvement in the state to the cooperation between conventional security agencies and the state’s home-grown security initiative, the Community Watch Corps.

He added that the state government had also “invested heavily” in non-kinetic interventions aimed at addressing some of the socio-economic factors that could fuel insecurity in the state.

The governor, therefore, appealed to security agencies and the media to be strategic in communicating security-related developments, warning against reports that could inadvertently amplify the activities of bandits and other criminal elements.

Radda urged the media to support security efforts by providing responsible coverage capable of boosting public confidence and the morale of security personnel operating in the northwest region of the country.

World.title: If OPay Is Going Public, Nigeria Should Be on the Ticket
World.content:
Shola Akande

If Bloomberg’s reporting proves correct, OPay could ring a bell in New York before the end of the year. The payments company, built on Nigerian consumers, Nigerian agents and Nigerian transactions, has reportedly engaged Citigroup, Deutsche Bank and JPMorgan for a potential United States listing targeting a valuation of around $4 billion.

That would be good news. It would be a powerful validation of what many of us have argued for years: Nigeria can produce businesses capable of competing for global capital at the highest level.

Nobody should begrudge OPay the deep capital pools, analyst coverage and international visibility that a New York listing can provide. Those advantages are real. But they should prompt a second question, rather than close the conversation.

Why not both?

A dual listing, New York for global capital and Lagos for the home market, is not a sentimental proposition. It is a commercial one. And the case rests on four things: customers, domestic liquidity, precedent and alignment.

The first is the customer.

OPay’s reported tens of millions of users are overwhelmingly Nigerian. They are the traders, artisans, students, small businesses and salary earners whose transactions helped build the franchise. A secondary listing on the Nigerian Exchange would give some of those customers the opportunity to become shareholders, converting economic participation into ownership.

Nigeria has already seen what happens when a major consumer-facing company deliberately broadens domestic ownership. MTN Nigeria’s public offer attracted more than 126,000 retail investors and created tens of thousands of new market accounts. The lesson is not that every shareholder becomes a brand ambassador. It is that a strong Nigerian consumer franchise can generate substantial domestic investor interest.

The second is liquidity.

Nigeria’s capital market is not the market it was a few years ago. The banking recapitalisation has demonstrated the depth of domestic institutional capital, while pension assets have continued to expand. The Exchange now has dedicated indices designed to support institutional investment, including the NGX Pension and NGX Pension Broad indices.

That matters because the argument for Lagos is no longer simply that Nigerians would like to own OPay. There is a potentially meaningful pool of domestic capital that could actually buy it.

Nigeria’s market infrastructure has also moved forward. The shift to T+1 settlement brought the equities settlement cycle in line with foreign markets including New York, reducing one important source of operational friction for international investors.

A Lagos listing would also give OPay access to naira-denominated demand and, depending on its eventual size and index eligibility, potentially broaden institutional demand through relevant domestic benchmarks. That is not a substitute for New York’s deeper pools of global capital. It is an additional source of liquidity and ownership.

The third is precedent. This road has been walked before.

Seplat has maintained a Lagos and London dual listing since 2014. Airtel Africa listed in London and subsequently in Lagos in 2019. Both demonstrated that a company can use an international market for global capital and visibility while retaining a meaningful connection to its home market.

The point is not that OPay should copy either company. It is that the supposed choice between international capital and domestic ownership is not a choice at all. The two can coexist.

The fourth is alignment.

OPay operates within Nigeria’s regulated payments ecosystem. The Central Bank of Nigeria lists OPay Digital Services as a licensed mobile money operator, while the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation lists it among insured mobile money operators. Its regulatory relationships, agent network and core customer base are deeply Nigerian. That creates a natural commercial argument for maintaining a visible presence in the country’s capital market.

But there is an important concession to make.

New York may well be the right primary market for OPay.

A company seeking a multibillion-dollar valuation may reasonably conclude that New York offers the deepest pool of fintech investors, the strongest international analyst coverage, the broadest universe of comparable companies and the most efficient access to global capital. If that is the conclusion, it should not be treated as a failure of the Nigerian market.

It should simply make the case for Lagos more precise.

Lagos does not need to beat New York. It needs to complement it.

A secondary Nigerian listing would allow OPay to establish a domestic ownership base without sacrificing the advantages of its international listing. New York could serve as the primary venue for global price discovery and international liquidity; Lagos could provide local institutional participation, retail ownership and a direct connection to the market in which much of the company’s economic story was created.

The two markets are complements, not competitors.

Some will argue that a dual listing creates additional compliance costs and administrative complexity. That is true. But it is precisely why the Nigerian market must continue making itself easier to access and operate in. Faster settlement, better market infrastructure, more efficient foreign-exchange processes and broader institutional participation are not cosmetic reforms. They determine whether companies view a domestic listing as a commercial decision or a patriotic sacrifice.

That distinction matters.

Because there is a bigger issue here than OPay’s eventual cap table.

Nigeria is entering a period in which some of its most successful businesses may begin contemplating the public markets. If the pattern becomes that our strongest companies build much of their scale here but list and raise their most consequential capital elsewhere, Nigeria risks exporting not just companies, but the wealth-creation opportunities attached to them.

The answer is not to compel companies to list at home. Nor is it to complain when founders and investors choose the markets that best serve their interests.

The answer is to make Nigeria’s capital market so competitive that listing here becomes the rational commercial choice.

Much of that work is already underway.

That is why OPay’s potential listing presents an opportunity beyond one company. It can become a test of whether Nigeria is prepared to capture more of the value created by the businesses emerging from its economy.

And it can set a precedent for the generation of Nigerian fintechs behind it: Moniepoint, Flutterwave and others that may eventually face similar decisions about accessing the public markets.

So this is not a criticism of OPay. It is an invitation to think bigger about what a successful public-market debut could look like.

Ring the bell in New York by all means, but there is a compelling case for ringing one in Lagos too.

The market is ready. The capital is waiting. And millions of Nigerians who already use the platform every day should have the opportunity, if they choose, to become owners of the company they helped build.

That would not be madness.

That would be the whole point.

* Akande, an economist, writes from Lagos

World.title: Let Ballot, Not Violence, Decide Osun Election, IPCR Warns
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The Institute for Peace and Conflict Resolution (IPCR) has warned political actors in Osun State against allowing violence, intimidation and inflammatory rhetoric to overshadow Saturday’s governorship election, urging all stakeholders to ensure that the ballot, rather than coercion, determines the choice of the people.

The warning came on Friday, less than 24 hours before voters in the state are scheduled to elect their governor, amid heightened concerns over election-related violence and security threats in parts of the state.

Recent security assessment have identified several Osun local government areas as vulnerable to electoral violence.

In a press statement by its Director-General, Dr. Joseph Ochogwu, the IPCR charged governorship candidates, political parties, their supporters, security agencies, election officials and voters to place the interest of Osun above partisan considerations.

The institute cautioned that political competition must not degenerate into violence, intimidation, threats, hate speech or destruction of property, stressing that political contests are temporary while the consequences of electoral violence could scar individuals, families and communities for years.

“Elections should not be treated as a do-or-die affair,” the Institute said, urging political leaders and candidates to demonstrate leadership by cautioning their supporters against inflammatory statements, misinformation and actions capable of escalating tensions.

The IPCR also delivered a clear message to candidates who may be dissatisfied with the outcome: accept the result peacefully or seek redress through the courts, rather than resorting to self-help.

It urged the candidates and political parties to respect the rules of democratic competition and demonstrate maturity before, during and after the election.

The institute equally called on voters to resist attempts by politicians or other actors to recruit them as agents of violence, urging them to exercise their civic responsibilities peacefully and respect the rights of citizens supporting rival political parties.

It advised voters to maintain order at polling units, respect election officials and security personnel, and avoid confrontations with political opponents.

The IPCR further warned citizens against becoming conduits for election-related misinformation, particularly on social media, urging them to verify information before sharing rumours or unconfirmed reports capable of triggering unrest.

The appeal comes against a backdrop of heightened tension in Osun, where reports of shootings, killings, clashes and other politically linked disturbances have fuelled concerns over the security of the August 15 poll.

A recent assessment by The Kukah Centre identified 15 local government areas as critical, high or moderate violence-risk zones, with Osogbo and Irewole classified as critical-risk areas.

The IPCR consequently charged security agencies to remain professional, impartial and respectful of citizens’ rights while ensuring adequate protection for voters, election officials and electoral materials.

It also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and its officials to discharge their responsibilities transparently and impartially, ensuring that eligible voters can cast their ballots without fear or intimidation.

Beyond the polling booths, the institute urged traditional rulers, religious leaders, community leaders, civil society organisations and the media to play their part in preventing violence and discouraging inflammatory rhetoric.

It stressed that the responsibility for a peaceful election does not rest solely with security agencies or INEC, but with every stakeholder participating in the electoral process.

The institute placed particular emphasis on the period after the announcement of results, urging winners to be magnanimous in victory and losers to accept defeat peacefully or pursue legitimate grievances through the judicial process.

The warning is particularly significant as Osun heads into Saturday’s contest after political parties had earlier signed a peace accord committing themselves to peaceful, free and credible elections.

The IPCR therefore called on the people of Osun State to protect the peace of their communities and demonstrate democratic maturity by ensuring that political differences do not become a trigger for bloodshed.

It said the ultimate test of the election would be whether the people are allowed to freely choose their governor without violence, intimidation or coercion.

“Let the ballot, rather than violence, intimidation or coercion, determine the choice of the people,” the Institute urged.

World.title: Bulls vs. All Blacks preview: Kiwis seek final tour tune-up at Loftus
World.content:
The Bulls host the All Blacks at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday in the final tour match before the Greatest Rivalry Test series begins.

The Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour reaches Pretoria on Saturday evening when a motivated Bulls side host the All Blacks at Loftus Versfeld, with both teams entering the match with something significant to prove.

For New Zealand, this is the last opportunity before the first Test against the Springboks at Ellis Park on 22 August. For the Bulls, it is a rare chance to test themselves against the world’s second-ranked side, and perhaps make history in the process.



A FAMOUS ANNIVERSARY LOOMS LARGE

Context matters enormously at Loftus this weekend. Saturday falls almost exactly on the 50th anniversary of Northern Transvaal’s famous 29-27 victory over the All Blacks in 1976, the last time a Bulls predecessor defeated New Zealand at this venue. That result occurred just weeks before Western Province’s equally celebrated win over the tourists in Cape Town, during a tour widely considered the most significant in South African rugby history.

The Bulls have won only once in four meetings with the All Blacks, but Johan Ackermann’s squad has been reminded of that historical precedent throughout the week. With the altitude of Loftus –1,350 metres above sea level – already providing a natural advantage, the home side has every reason to believe an upset is not beyond them.

“Loftus Versfeld is one of the most formidable rugby grounds in the world,” All Blacks coach Dave Rennie acknowledged. “We are aware of the challenge in front of us and excited at what lies ahead.”

BULLS BLEND EXPERIENCE WITH NEW ARRIVALS

Ackermann has named a quite competitive squad despite the absence of several Springboks on international duty. Captain Marcell Coetzee leads a match-day squad that includes five other capped Boks in the form of Willie le Roux, Curwin Bosch, Embrose Papier, Elrigh Louw and Johan Grobbelaar. Scrumhalf Papier, the URC’s joint-leading try scorer last season with 12, will control the tempo alongside flyhalf Bosch, a player making his first appearance for the Bulls after two years in France.

Bosch’s instinctive attacking game and eye for space could be a significant weapon against an All Blacks side that has at times struggled to contain enterprising pivot play on this tour. Loose forward Hanro Liebenberg, back on South African soil after spending five seasons at the Leicester Tigers, adds further menace across the back row alongside the ever-reliable Jeandre Rudolph, who forced 15 turnovers during last season’s URC campaign.

Louw and Grobbelaar were released from the Springboks squad and added to the Bulls bench, though both have had only a single training session with the team since returning from Argentina.



ALL BLACKS MAKING FINAL AUDITIONS COUNT

Rennie has made 19 changes from the side that crushed the Sharks 54-0 on Tuesday, but these selection were made on purpose. Tour captain Codie Taylor makes his first appearance of Rugby’s Greatest Rugby Rivalry, while Beauden Barrett moves to fullback after a difficult outing at flyhalf against the Stormers. The 144-cap veteran should be more comfortable with time and space in the back-field rather than the decision-making pressure of the No 10 jersey.

Wings Josh Moorby and Leroy Carter are both playing for Test spots with Will Jordan’s fitness uncertain for next weekend’s series opener against the Springboks. Peter Lakai, Anton Segner and Simon Parker form a new loose forward combination with points to prove, while uncapped flyhalf Josh Jacomb gets his first extended opportunity against competitive provincial opposition.

Assistant coach Tana Umaga has been vocal about the need to play with greater pace to speed the game up.

“What is this game that we want to put out to our public?” Umaga said this week. “I think we’re doing everything we cannot to do it.”

Saturday offers a chance to demonstrate precisely that against a Bulls side built to slow things down.

MATCH PREDICTION

The Bulls have the forward pack and the set-piece quality to make this a genuine contest. Their lineout and scrum statistics edge New Zealand’s, and altitude invariably flattens visiting teams’ fitness advantages in the final quarter. Ackermann’s squad also contains considerably more combined experience than the Sharks side that was overwhelmed in Durban.

However, the All Blacks’ attacking statistics remain exceptional. They have scored at least 34 points in every 2026 outing and have genuine Test-class players throughout their lineup for this clash. While the second half, when altitude bites, will be the defining period, expect the men in black to clinch victory after a stern test against the Bulls.

World.title: Frans Steyn: Where the two-time World Cup winner is today
World.content:
Frans Steyn was a marvel to watch during his playing days and became renowned for his extraordinary long-range kicking ability.

Having made his professional debut as a teenager, Steyn quickly established himself as one of the most exciting players in world rugby during the late 2000s.

His immense physical strength, versatility, pinpoint kicking and remarkable longevity made him a key figure for both the Springboks and the teams he represented at club level.



Although Steyn began his professional career with the Sharks, he spent much of his playing career outside South Africa. He spent seven years in France, playing for Racing 92 and Montpellier, and also enjoyed a three-year stint in Japan.

Frans Steyn played majority of his rugby overseas

In 2020, Steyn returned to South Africa for the first time in 11 years and joined the Cheetahs. However, a knee injury in 2023 ultimately brought an end to his illustrious playing career.

Steyn’s Springboks legacy

Steyn arguably made his biggest impact on the international stage with the Springboks.

The versatile back was known for his ability to consistently slot long-range penalties and produce spectacular drop goals from distances of 55 metres and beyond.

He played a crucial role in South Africa‘s 2007 Rugby World Cup triumph. At just 20 years old, Steyn featured prominently in the final against England, contributing in both attack and defence.

He also produced one of the final’s most memorable moments when he calmly converted a 48-metre penalty in the 62nd minute, extending South Africa’s lead to 15-6.



That victory saw Steyn become the youngest player to win a Rugby World Cup. He was just 20 years and 159 days old when he lifted the Webb Ellis Cup.

Steyn went on to enjoy an extraordinary international career, earning 78 Springboks caps over 12 years. He added a second Rugby World Cup winners’ medal in 2019 as South Africa defeated England in the final in Japan.

Where is Frans Steyn today?

Following his retirement from professional rugby in 2023, Steyn immediately moved into coaching and management.

The Springboks icon was appointed Director of Rugby at the Cheetahs before later taking charge as head coach of the Free State side.

His transition into coaching has allowed him to remain involved in the game and pass on the experience he gained during an illustrious career that included two Rugby World Cup triumphs.

Away from rugby, Steyn is married to Linca, and the couple have three daughters.

While his playing career may be over, Frans Steyn remains closely involved in South African rugby and continues to build the next chapter of his career from the sidelines.

Which version of Steyn was the best? 2007 or 2019?

World.title: More pensioners now qualify for full rates rebate
World.content:
Cape Town pensioners living as Life Right Holders in separately valued Sectional Title Schemes now have a new avenue to slash their municipal rates bills, as the City expands its pensioner rebate relief programme.

Residents older than 60 who are Life Right Holders in separately valued sectional title properties may now apply for rates relief, provided their household income does not exceed R27 000 a month. This is a significant increase from previous qualifying thresholds, opening the door to far more pensioners than before.

Those in freehold Life Right properties will have to wait roughly six months while their properties undergo a separate valuation process, after which applications will open for them too. For SASSA beneficiaries and other grant recipients stretching every rand of their monthly income, this expanded threshold could mean the difference between falling short and finally qualifying for meaningful relief.



How much you could save as a pensioner

The rebate works on a sliding scale. Pensioners earning between R0 and R10 000 a month qualify for a 100% rates rebate, while those earning between R24 001 and R27 000 receive a 10% rebate, with a graduated scale in between. The benefit runs for roughly three years, aligned with the City’s General Valuation cycle, though scheme administrators or property owners must confirm annually that the applicant still occupies the property.

What you need to apply and key deadlines

Applicants must submit a completed ‘Rates Rebate for Life Rights Holders’ form, signed by both the Life Right Holder and the property owner or company representative. Also required: certified ID copies of the applicant and spouse or partner, a copy of the Life Right agreement, proof of income (pension slips, rental income, investments or dividends), and three months of bank statements for all accounts. Applications can be submitted in person at any Revenue Customer Interaction Centre or emailed to Rates.Rebate@capetown.gov.za.

Pensioners renewing existing rebates face strict cut-off dates. Those who applied before 1 July will have their benefits backdated once approved. Anyone applying after that date must finalise their renewal by 31 August to receive backdated relief; those who miss the deadline will forfeit their discount until approval comes through.



The City has set aside more than R8,3 billion in social assistance for qualifying pensioners and indigent residents for the 2026/27 financial year.

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Property prices up 30% in this coastal town where retirees buy half the homes
World.content:
A sunny day on the South Coast. Image: Pexels

In the last year, property prices in Trafalgar on KwaZulu-Natal’s South Coast have increased 30%.

This rise means this small town is beating the likes of major metros like Cape Town.

The increase is nearly four times the national average and eight times higher than KwaZulu-Natal’s average.



Property prices jumped 30% in one year

According to Property24, the average property price for Trafalgar in 2025 was R665 000; the most recent data puts this at R892 000, a 34.2% increase.

Forty-five properties have sold this year, 2 more than in 2024 and only 3 fewer than in 2025.

Buyers over 50 account for 57.7% of the town’s house sales. The over-50s also make up 77.3% of Trafalgar’s property owners.

Data from Property 24 shows 30 properties were sold between June and July.

Why are retirees buying homes in Trafalgar?

KwaZulu-Natal’s South Coast has been booming since the start of the year.

Data suggests Trafalgar’s cost-effective pricing may play a role in its success.



In neighbouring San Lameer, 28 properties have sold since the start of the year. The average house price is R1.45 million.

In Palm Beach, 38 homes have sold since the start of the year. The average house price is R756 000, lower than in Trafalgar.

Yet, Palm Beach seems to be attracting a younger crowd. Buyers aged 18 to 35 make up 23.5% of the region’s home sales.

Retirees may also be choosing Trafalgar because of the town’s comforts.

Residents have access to Trafalgar Beach, a Blue Flag beach, one of only nine beaches that have been awarded this status in KwaZulu-Natal.

The beach remains unspoiled because of the Trafalgar Marine Protected Zone (TMPZ), a 6-kilometre zone that includes Trafalgar Beach.

Hardy Avenue, the farthest road from the beach, is only a 15-minute walk or 3-minute drive from Trafalgar Beach.

Then there’s Mpenjati Nature Reserve, where residents can bird watch, hike, fish, and swim.

Cost of Buying Property in Trafalgar

Item Price (2026) Average Home R892 000 Average Sectional Title R1.3 million Average Erven R865 000 Rates R340 – R4 400

Trafalgar Crime Statistics

Yet, retirees moving to the area have to contend with crime.

Trafalgar is part of Port Edward, where crime increased 8.4% year-on-year.

According to data from the South African Police Service (SAPS), property crime is up 17.5%.

There were 172 house break-ins in Port Edward between April 2025 and March 2026.

This data shows figures from Port Edward, which, besides Trafalgar, includes Leisure Bay, Munster, WaNzimakwe, Mgangathe, and Port Edward.

Precise data about crime in Trafalgar isn’t reported.

World.title: El Niño heatwave, or an El Niño water crisis?
World.content:
South Africa's dams look healthy today, but a strengthening El Niño could change that fast this summer: Image ChatGPT

The El Niño water risk is what readers pushed back on when we covered South Africa’s shift from this week’s cold snap toward a strengthening El Niño, insisting heat isn’t really the concern…

Water is.

Here’s what the data actually says about that risk.



Why the El Niño water risk matters more than healthy dam levels suggest

As of early August, South Africa’s dams sit at a reassuring 95.9% full nationally, with the Western Cape’s average at 79.6% and North West leading at 102.4%.

But climate researchers warn that healthy dam levels now say very little about what a strong El Niño summer could do to them.

Extreme heat dramatically accelerates evaporation, acting like a sponge that pulls untreated water straight out of open dams and reservoirs, often without a single drop reaching a tap or a field.



Why El Niño hits South Africa’s water system twice over

El Niño typically brings both delayed rainfall and higher temperatures to South Africa’s summer rainfall regions, a combination that compounds rather than simply adds up.

Underground aquifers recharge slowly, so sustained dry spells can cause boreholes to run dry or turn saline.

The World Meteorological Organisation’s latest seasonal update shows sea surface temperatures in the key Niño 3.4 region climbing toward roughly 2.9°C above average by October, with the event expected to peak around November.



Exactly as South Africa heads into the heart of summer.

The Day Zero comparison experts keep bringing up

Cape Town’s 2018 Day Zero crisis is the reference point climate experts keep returning to, a reminder of how quickly healthy-looking dam levels can unravel under sustained heat and low rainfall.

Farmers, agribusinesses and municipalities are already being urged to build in buffer capacity now, rather than waiting for restrictions to force the issue later in the season.



It’s easy to look at 95% full dams and think we’re in the clear, hey, but if this El Niño plays out the way forecasters expect, that number could look very different by autumn.

2018 was hectic, I really hope we don’t see a repeat of that in 2026.

Do you think water restrictions are a bigger risk than the heat itself this summer?



Let us know in the comments below, Mzansi…

World.title: Zambia stops election vote count amid violence fears
World.content:
Zambia has suspended the counting and announcement of election results nationwide after the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) reported violence targeting polling staff and the alleged theft of marked ballot papers.

The commission announced the suspension on Friday, a day after Zambians voted in presidential, parliamentary and local government elections.

The nation held presidential, parliamentary and local government elections on Thursday.



The ECZ said it had received reports of violence “during the counting and announcement of results in some districts”.

It said the violence was “targeted at Poll staff” and, in some cases, had resulted in “the theft of marked ballot papers in ballot boxes”.

The commission said it had acted because of the security situation and continued threats of violence.

“In view of the security situation and continued threats of violence,” the ECZ said it had “with immediate effect suspended the counting and announcement of results throughout the country”.

The commission cited Section 67 (3) of the Electoral Process Act No. 35 of 2016 as the legal basis for the suspension.

Electoral Commission of Zambia to review suspension

The suspension has put the brakes on the counting process as Zambia waits for the outcome of a closely watched presidential election.



The said it would review the decision within 24 hours.

“The Commission will review the suspension within 24 hours,” it said.

Counting began shortly after polling stations closed on Thursday, but no official presidential results had been announced when the commission halted the process.

The ECZ had previously expected to complete the announcement of the presidential results by Monday.

Opposition raises concerns over delays

The suspension came shortly after opposition candidate Brian Mundubile expressed “grave concern” over delays in announcing the presidential results.

Mundubile warned that prolonged delays could create opportunities for interference or manipulation.

He also cited what he described as “deeply troubling reports” from several areas, including alleged military involvement at tallying centres and concerns about the movement of ballot boxes.

Mundubile called for the immediate publication of results on a polling-station-by-polling-station basis.

He also called for the protection of the chain of custody of ballot materials and investigations into the reported incidents.

Hichilema urges Zambians to remain calm

President Hakainde Hichilema, who is seeking a second five-year term, has urged Zambians to remain calm while the electoral authorities handle the situation.

Hichilema faces 13 challengers, with Mundubile regarded as one of his main opponents.

The president urged citizens to remain “peaceful, patient and patriotic” as they await the official outcome from the authorities managing the election.

The ECZ’s decision has now created uncertainty over when Zambia will receive the official election results, with the commission first needing to assess the security situation before deciding whether to resume counting.

World.title: Banyana keep Brazil 2027 World Cup hopes alive

JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's Banyana Banyana kept their hopes alive of qualifying for the Women's World Cup Brazil year.

After defeating Nigeria 2-1 in their WAFCON play-in match, Banyana will serve as CAF's one of two teams alongside Ghana in the Play-Off's, which will be begin in November and December of this year and be completed in February 2027.

Ghana's Black Queens eliminated the Ivory Coast.

World.title: TikTok strangers rally to reunite Cape Town student with mother battling cancer
World.content:
PIETERMARITZBURG - What started as a tearful TikTok plea for strangers to visit her mother, who is being treated for cancer at a KwaZulu-Natal hospital, has turned into a remarkable story of kindness.

Earlier this week, Londiwe Molefe, originally from Newcastle, posted a tearful video on TikTok asking people to visit her mother at Greys Hospital in Pietermaritzburg.

Unable to afford the trip from Cape Town, Molefe said she feared her mother was not doing well and had no one else to check on her.

Her plea, which attracted more than 5,000 comments, struck a chord with the app's users.

“My mom was admitted at Greys Hospital. I’m currently in Cape Town and there is no one at home who can go check on her,” Molefe said in the video.

“I don’t have another option. She is not okay. If anyone is close to Greys or can visit her, please go. Even just five minutes with her would mean the world and make her feel so much better.”

Molefe’s followers responded to her plea, with one offering to buy her a plane ticket so she could travel to KwaZulu-Natal and be reunited with her mother. Many others flocked to Greys hospital to visit her mother.

On Wednesday, Molefe arrived in Pietermaritzburg and was also able to visit her mother. Another user also offered her a place to stay, while another good samaritan paid for her return ticket back to Cape Town.

Reflecting on the outpouring of support, Molefe thanked those who had donated, visited her mother on her behalf and offered emotional support.

“When I made the video about my mom being in hospital, I never imagined it would touch so many of you. Thank you for the donations. Thank you for going to see my mom on my behalf. Thank you for calling me, for the messages, for sacrificing your time,” she wrote.

“Because of your kindness, I am able to go to KZN to see my mom too. You carried me when I felt so broken. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.”

World.title: ‘A full-circle moment’: Gabi Motuba reflects on Standard Bank Joy of Jazz journey

JOHANNESBURG – Standard Bank Young Artist winner Gabi Motuba says performing alongside American jazz vocalist Kurt Elling at the 2026 Standard Bank Joy of Jazz will be a full circle moment.

The Mamelodi-raised artist has been named among the top artists who serenade music lovers at this year’s festival set to take place on 25 and 26 September.

The lineup features global and South African stars including Floetry, Angélique Kidjo, McCoy Mrubata and Thandiswa Mazwai among others.

“It’s incredible. It’s quite surreal experience,” Motuba told eNCA.

“I remember going to one of the Joy of Jazz concerts and watching Kurt Elling, and now I’m on that very spot. It’s such a full circle moment for me because that was such a significant experience.”

Motuba will perform songs from her recent musical project Sounds from a Black Girl, which is a mix of neo soul and improvision.

“This offering is a meditation on affirmations. After coming from a sabbath themed around grief, I’m lucky to have come out on the other side. This is the tone of the album. I want it to arm young girls for a world that is not always accepting.”

World.title: 'Shock' gloves for US immigration agents fuel potential abuse fears
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Plans to equip US immigration enforcement agents with gloves capable of delivering debilitating electric shocks have fueled concerns over potential abuses by a force that critics say is already overzealous and under-trained.

"As if assaulting people and shooting people in the streets wasn't enough," Representative Maxwell Frost, a Democrat from Florida, said on X. "Now, they're spending $20 million of YOUR taxpayer dollars on painful electric shock gloves for their masked, lawless goons."

"ICE must be stopped," Frost said in a reference to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the agency primarily charged with carrying out President Donald Trump's plan to deport millions of undocumented migrants.

ICE has come in for criticism for a series of fatal shootings during enforcement operations, including those of two American citizens in Minnesota in January who were involved in anti-ICE protests.

Critics have focused on the forceful tactics used by ICE agents in rounding up migrants and on an alleged lowering of the standards of training for new recruits.

The plan to purchase the shock gloves, which was first reported by The Associated Press, calls for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the ICE parent agency, to spend $10 to $20 million on what are described as "distraction and de-escalation" devices.

The G.L.O.V.E., or Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter, is made by Compliant Technologies, a company based in Kentucky that bills itself on its website as a supplier of "cutting-edge non-lethal tools to empower and protect those who serve."

The G.L.O.V.E. delivers a shock that is not as strong as that of a Taser, another device used by law enforcement to subdue suspects.

In response to queries about the gloves, DHS said ICE is "constantly assessing the needs of our officers in the field to ensure they have the tools and equipment necessary to safely arrest and remove criminal illegal aliens from our country."

"Every decision is made with careful consideration and appropriately reviewed to ensure that any technology ICE utilises is consistent with all applicable law enforcement policies and standards," DHS said in a statement.

- 'Misused' -

John Sandweg, who served as the acting ICE director under Democratic president Barack Obama, said in an interview with MS NOW that ICE agents have an "incredibly difficult job" but expressed concerns about the electric gloves.

"Deploying this admittedly less-than-lethal technology, in an era when we're really not all that interested in providing training to the officers about how to use that technology, really is alarming," Sandweg said.

"It doesn't take a big stretch of the imagination to see this technology being deployed against a mother who's just maybe putting up the mildest resistance because she's being separated from her children," he said. "It's too easy for this to get misused against a population that doesn't pose a threat."

Representative Pramila Jayapal, a Democrat from Washington state, expressed similar concerns.

"ICE has targeted legal observers, protestors, and just ordinary people on their way to work or to drop their kid off at school," Jayapal said on X. "This won't make anyone safer and in fact just gives ICE another dangerous tool to target citizens and immigrants alike."

The American Civil Liberties Union announced last month that it has filed more than 50 claims against the federal government on behalf of people and families allegedly harmed by federal immigration actions in 17 states and in Washington, the nation's capital.

ICE arrested more than 51,000 people for immigration violations across the country in July, according to US media reports citing DHS sources, the most in a single month since Trump took office in January of last year.

World.title: Relief for Kenyans as EPRA announces reduced fuel prices
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The government has extended relief to motorists and industries with a Sh5 drop in diesel prices in the latest fuel pricing cycle.

The prices of super petrol and kerosene have, however, been retained as they are by the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA).

As such, a litre of diesel will retail at Sh217.86 in Nairobi while super petrol remains at Sh214.03 a litre and kerosene Sh191.38 a litre.

“In the period under review, the maximum allowed petroleum pump prices for diesel decreases by Sh5/litre while the price of super petrol and kerosene remain unchanged due to additional government stabilisation support measures of Sh938 million,” said EPRA Acting Director General Dr Eng Joseph Oketch.

The drop is seen as a move by the government to tame runaway inflation that settled at 6.5 per cent in July. The drop may result in softening of prices of industrial based commodities, particularly food items.

This is considering that food inflation is a significant contributor to spikes in the overall inflation figures.
